name: Dough & Co
short_description: Wood-fired sourdough pizza from a converted horse trailer. Hackney-born, London-obsessed.
long_description: We started Dough & Co in a Hackney Wick car park in 2018 with a second-hand Valoriani oven and zero business plan. Five years later we've done 400+ weddings and we still make every base by hand that morning. Our dough gets a 48-hour cold ferment — it's the kind of chewy, blistered crust that makes you close your eyes. We bring the full setup: the trailer, the oven, the playlist, and enough nduja honey pizza to keep your uncle happy. We do classic Margheritas, seasonal specials (wild garlic in spring, truffle in winter), and a vegan menu that doesn't feel like an afterthought.
pricing_notes: Minimum spend £600, then £12-15 per head. Includes 3 pizza choices, salad, and service. Dessert pizzas extra.
setup_requirements: Flat hard-standing area 5m x 3m. No power needed — we're self-contained with gas and wood. Outdoor or covered outdoor only.
peak_season: May to September — book early for summer Saturdays
signature_items: Nduja & honey pizza with fresh chilli
founder_story: Started by two ex-architects who quit their jobs after a pizza-making holiday in Naples and never looked back.
reviews_sample: Booked them for our wedding in June — guests are STILL talking about the pizzas. The nduja honey one is life-changing. — Sarah, wedding
Best corporate event food we've ever had. Setup was seamless, the team were lovely. — Mark, corporate summer party
We've used them twice now for birthdays. The kids go absolutely mad for the dessert pizzas. — Priya, 40th birthday
booking_notes: Happy to do tasting sessions for weddings (£50, redeemable against booking). Can do late-night service until 11pm. Minimum 2 hours on site.

name: Ember & Smoke
short_description: Low and slow BBQ from a custom-built smoker. Brisket that's been cooking since yesterday.
long_description: We're obsessed with fire and time. Our brisket goes on at 4am — 14 hours over cherry wood — and by the time your guests arrive it's falling apart. We built our smoker from scratch in a railway arch in Tottenham, and we haul it to weddings, festivals, and garden parties across London. The menu is Texan at heart but London in spirit: think smoked short rib with a gochujang glaze, or pulled pork with a scotch bonnet slaw. We're not a burger van with some smoke on the side — this is proper pit BBQ, and we bring the whole theatre of it. Your guests will smell us before they see us.
pricing_notes: £18-25 per head depending on menu. Minimum spend £1,200. Includes setup, service, and breakdown. Sides and desserts can be added.
setup_requirements: Need 6m x 4m outdoor space. We bring our own smoker and gas. Can do covered outdoor but not fully indoor. Water access helpful but not essential.
peak_season: June to September, but we love a winter feast too
signature_items: Pulled pork with scotch bonnet slaw
founder_story: Founded by a former chef at The Smokehouse Islington who wanted to bring proper American pit BBQ to London events.
reviews_sample: The brisket was genuinely the best thing I've ever eaten at a wedding. People were going back for thirds. — James, wedding
Hired them for a 50th — the smoker arriving was a spectacle in itself. Food was incredible. — Helen, 50th birthday
They catered our company summer party. 150 people, zero complaints, multiple requests for their number. — Tom, corporate event
booking_notes: Tasting sessions available for events over £2k. Can pair with a dessert vendor if needed. We bring our own lighting for evening events.

name: Little Bao Boy
primary_category: bao, dumplings, and Asian street food
short_description: Steamed bao buns and dumplings from a neon-lit street food truck. Stoke Newington's worst-kept secret.
long_description: We've been slinging bao from our truck on Church Street since 2020, and we've built a proper cult following. Every bun is hand-folded that morning — pillowy, slightly sweet, and stuffed until it can barely close. The pork belly with pickled daikon is our bestseller, but honestly the mushroom & truffle bao converts more meat-eaters than anything we've ever made. For events, we set up a steaming station that's basically dinner and a show: clouds of steam, neon signage, and a queue that makes your party look popular. We also do dumpling platters for more formal dos.
pricing_notes: £10-14 per head for 3-bao meal. Dumpling platters from £8 per head. Minimum spend £500.
setup_requirements: 3m x 2m space, access to power (13amp socket). Can work indoors or outdoors. We bring our own steamers, neon sign, and serving station.
peak_season: Year-round — bao don't care about weather
signature_items: Pork belly bao with pickled daikon & hoisin
Crispy duck bao with spring onion & plum sauce
founder_story: Run by siblings Danny and Mei, who grew up making dumplings with their grandmother in her Dalston kitchen every Sunday.
reviews_sample: The mushroom bao is unreal — I'm not even vegan and I ordered three. Perfect party food. — Aisha, 30th birthday
Booked for a christening, everyone was obsessed. The neon sign made for great photos too. — Chris, christening
Our office can't stop talking about the dumplings. Already rebooked for Christmas. — Jen, corporate event
booking_notes: Neon sign available for photos (says 'EAT BAO'). Can do canapé-style mini bao for formal events. Tasting for events over £1k.

name: The Grazing Collective
short_description: Showstopping grazing tables built on-site. Charcuterie, cheese, and more cheese.
long_description: We build grazing tables that make people stop and take a photo before they eat. Every board is assembled on-site — we arrive two hours early, lay everything out on olive wood boards and vintage platters, and create something that looks like it belongs in a magazine. We source from Neal's Yard, Brindisa, and small producers we've found at farmers' markets over the years. Our signature is the 'mile-long' table: a continuous spread that runs the length of your venue. We also do boxed grazing for more structured events, and we're brilliant at dietary requirements — our vegan boards are just as stunning as the classic charcuterie.
pricing_notes: From £15 per head (small boards) to £30 per head (full mile-long table). Minimum spend £300. Includes setup, styling, and all serving ware.
setup_requirements: Table or surface to build on (we can bring trestle tables if needed). Indoor preferred. Need access 2 hours before guests arrive.
peak_season: Wedding season (May-Sep) and Christmas party season (Nov-Dec)
founder_story: Founded by food stylist Camille who got tired of making food look good for cameras and decided to make it look good for actual people.
reviews_sample: Our wedding guests literally gasped when they saw the table. Worth every penny. — Laura, wedding
Booked for a baby shower — the vegan board was so beautiful I felt bad eating it. Almost. — Nadia, baby shower
Best corporate lunch we've ever done. The boxes were stunning and the team were so professional. — Rachel, corporate event
booking_notes: Free consultation for events over £500. Can coordinate with florists for table styling. All boards are compostable or reusable — nothing goes to landfill.

name: Mr Whippy Don't Know Me
primary_category: ice cream vans and gelato carts
short_description: Proper gelato from a pastel-pink vintage van. Not your average 99.
long_description: We're the antidote to sad ice cream vans with broken jingles. Our 1972 Bedford van (Dolly) has been restored in blush pink and serves proper Italian gelato made fresh in our Dalston kitchen. Every flavour is churned in small batches — we're talking Sicilian pistachio, salted caramel with honeycomb shards, and a rotating seasonal special (strawberry & basil in summer, gingerbread in winter). For events, Dolly pulls up looking like a dream, we hang the bunting, and suddenly your garden party has a centrepiece. We also do affogato bars, gelato sandwiches, and build-your-own sundae stations for the extra crowd.
pricing_notes: From £400 for 2 hours (up to 80 scoops). Then £4 per head. Unlimited service packages available for weddings.
setup_requirements: Vehicle access to site. Flat ground for the van. Self-contained — no power needed. Outdoor or large indoor spaces.
peak_season: April to September, but we do winter events with hot chocolate add-ons
founder_story: Gina spent three summers working in a gelateria in Bologna, came home, found a rusting Bedford on eBay, and the rest is Instagram history.
reviews_sample: Dolly was the highlight of our wedding. The pistachio gelato is absurd. — Kate, wedding
Every kid at the school fête went back for seconds (and thirds). Parents too. — David, school fête
Hired for a corporate summer party — the van looked incredible and the affogato station was genius. — Sophie, corporate event
booking_notes: Dolly is very popular for weddings — book 3+ months ahead for summer Saturdays. Custom flavours available for events over £800. We bring bunting, chalkboard menus, and compostable cups.

name: Taco Loco
short_description: Proper corn tortilla tacos from a bright yellow truck. No hard shells, no nonsense.
long_description: We press our tortillas fresh on-site — you can hear them hitting the plancha from across the garden. Our corn comes from a nixtamal supplier in Brixton, and everything else follows that same logic: if we can make it from scratch, we do. Al pastor on the vertical spit, carnitas braised for six hours, and a black bean & sweet potato taco that's so good vegetarians forget they're eating the 'option'. We're loud, we're colourful, and we turn every event into a street party. The truck is painted Oaxacan yellow, we hang papel picado from whatever we can find, and we play cumbia until someone tells us to stop.
pricing_notes: £12-16 per head for 3 tacos, rice, slaw, and salsa. Minimum spend £550. Margarita bar add-on available.
setup_requirements: 5m x 3m space for the truck. Self-contained with gas. Outdoor or covered outdoor. We bring our own lighting and music.
peak_season: Summer, but tacos work year-round — we've done plenty of winter weddings
signature_items: Al pastor from the vertical spit with pineapple & coriander
Elote (grilled corn with mayo, chilli, lime)
founder_story: Carlos left a desk job in finance after a three-month trip through Mexico, bought a truck, and taught himself to make tortillas from YouTube and his abuela's voice notes.
reviews_sample: The al pastor was insane. Watching them carve it off the spit was a whole vibe. — Ollie, 30th birthday
Booked for our garden wedding — the truck, the music, the food. Absolutely perfect. — Zara, wedding
Best tacos I've had outside of Mexico City. And I've been to Mexico City. — Liam, private party
booking_notes: Margarita bar is £8 per head on top. Churros dessert add-on £3 per head. We bring our own Bluetooth speaker and papel picado decorations.

name: Flat White Events
short_description: Speciality coffee cart for events. Proper espresso, not conference-room brown water.
long_description: We exist because nobody should have to drink bad coffee at their own wedding. Our cart is a converted timber-and-brass setup that looks like a tiny third-wave café dropped into your venue. We pull shots on a La Marzocca Linea Mini, use beans from Assembly and Origin, and our baristas actually know what they're doing — latte art included. We do morning-after-the-wedding brunches, post-ceremony pick-me-ups, and corporate events where the coffee is finally better than the small talk. We've also added a pastry package with croissants from a bakery in Clapton, because coffee without pastry is just sad.
pricing_notes: From £350 for 2 hours (up to 60 coffees). Unlimited packages from £6 per head. Pastry add-on £4 per head.
setup_requirements: 1.5m x 1m space, access to a 13amp power socket. Indoor or outdoor. We bring filtered water.
peak_season: Year-round — weddings in summer, corporate in autumn/winter
signature_items: Hot chocolate with real chocolate shavings
founder_story: Ex-barista champion Seb got tired of watching caterers serve instant coffee at beautiful weddings and decided to fix it.
reviews_sample: Had them for the morning after our wedding — everyone was so grateful for proper coffee with their hangover. — Amy, wedding
The cart looked gorgeous in our office. Best team event we've done. — Dan, corporate
Croissants and flat whites for my baby shower. Simple and perfect. — Mia, baby shower
booking_notes: Latte art for every cup. Custom cup sleeves available for weddings (your names/date). Can add espresso martini service for evening events.

name: The Falafel Guys
short_description: Crispy falafel wraps and loaded mezze platters. Everything made from scratch, nothing from a packet.
long_description: We started on Broadway Market in 2019 with a tiny stall and a recipe from Omar's mum. Four years later we've catered weddings, corporate dos, and one very memorable bar mitzvah where we served 300 people and ran out of nothing. Our falafel is made fresh every morning — chickpeas soaked overnight, blended with coriander, cumin, and a bit of baking soda for that perfect crispy shell. The shawarma is marinated for 24 hours and carved to order. But honestly, the thing people lose their minds over is the sides: our baba ganoush is smoky and silky, the fattoush has the crunchiest pita chips, and the garlic sauce is so good people ask for a pot to take home.
pricing_notes: £8-12 per head for wraps and mezze. Minimum spend £400. Sharing-style mezze platters from £15 per head.
setup_requirements: 3m x 2m space. We need one 13amp socket. Can work indoors or out. Bring our own fryer and grill.
peak_season: Year-round, busiest May-September
signature_items: Crispy falafel wrap with tahini & pickled turnip
founder_story: Omar and his brother Tariq started with their mum's falafel recipe and a market stall. She still taste-tests every batch.
reviews_sample: Best falafel I've had in London, no exaggeration. And the garlic sauce haunts my dreams. — Ella, birthday party
Fed 80 people at our engagement party for under a grand. Everyone was stuffed and happy. — Ravi, engagement party
We hire them for our office quarterly lunches now. Nobody complains about the food anymore. — Lucy, corporate
booking_notes: Halal certified. Happy to do tasting for events over £600. Can provide sharing-style mezze platters as starters alongside a main caterer.

name: Patty Smith
short_description: Smashed burgers and dirty fries from a matte-black truck. Not fancy, just really bloody good.
long_description: We do one thing and we do it properly: double-smashed patties on a Martin's potato bun with American cheese, pickles, and our secret sauce. That's it. No truffle. No wagyu for the sake of it. Just a technically perfect burger cooked on a plancha so hot it gets a crust in 45 seconds. We added a fried chicken burger last year because people kept asking, and now it outsells the beef on Fridays. The fries are hand-cut, double-fried, and come loaded if you want them (bacon, cheese sauce, jalapeños, spring onion). We work fast — we've served 200 people in under 90 minutes — and we leave the site cleaner than we found it.
pricing_notes: £10-14 per head for burger, fries, and a drink. Minimum spend £500. Loaded fries upgrade £3.
setup_requirements: 5m x 3m for the truck. Flat hard-standing. Self-contained — no power needed. Outdoor only (or with extraction).
peak_season: Summer festivals and party season, but honestly we're busy year-round
signature_items: Double smash burger with secret sauce
Fried chicken burger with slaw & hot honey
reviews_sample: Best burgers we've had at any event. Simple, no fuss, absolutely perfect. The queue didn't stop. — Jake, festival
Hired for my husband's 40th and he said it was the best birthday present. High praise. — Noor, 40th birthday
Fast, clean, professional. 150 burgers in just over an hour. Legendary. — Alex, corporate summer party
booking_notes: Can turn around bookings in as little as 48 hours for smaller events. Veggie/vegan options available on request. Late-night service until midnight.

name: Spice Box
short_description: Indian street food with a London twist. Chaat, dosa, and the best dal you'll eat this year.
long_description: We grew up eating chaat on Drummond Street and dosa at Diwana. Spice Box is our love letter to that food — proper Indian street food made from family recipes but served in a way that works at a London wedding or a Shoreditch office party. Our dosa station is the showstopper: we pour the batter in front of your guests, fill it with spiced potato, and serve it with three chutneys. The chaat is assembled to order — papdi, yoghurt, tamarind, pomegranate, coriander, sev — each one a tiny flavour bomb. And our dal makhani has been slow-cooking since last night. We're entirely vegetarian, with a full vegan menu that doesn't compromise on flavour.
pricing_notes: £12-18 per head depending on menu. Minimum spend £600. Dosa station add-on £4 per head. Chai station £3 per head.
setup_requirements: 3m x 3m space, one 13amp socket. Dosa station needs flat surface. Indoor or outdoor. We bring our own tawa and equipment.
peak_season: Wedding season and Diwali period (October-November)
signature_items: Live dosa station with potato masala & three chutneys
Masala chai from a brass samovar
founder_story: Run by sisters Anita and Priya, third-generation cooks who learned at their grandmother's elbow in Southall and decided London events deserved better Indian food.
reviews_sample: The dosa station was the moment of our wedding. Guests were mesmerised watching them being made. — Deepa, wedding
Best Indian food I've had at any event. The chaat was perfect — every bite was different. — Will, 40th birthday
We're a predominantly vegetarian company and Spice Box absolutely nailed it. Everyone ate well. — Meera, corporate event
The chai samovar was such a lovely touch at our baby shower. Felt really special. — Sonia, baby shower
booking_notes: Fully vegetarian kitchen — no cross-contamination concerns. Chai samovar is incredibly popular for winter events. Tasting available for events over £1k.

name: Pie Minister
short_description: Hand-crimped pies, proper mash, and lashings of gravy. Comfort food for every occasion.
long_description: We make pies the way your nan would if your nan had trained at Le Cordon Bleu. Butter pastry, slow-cooked fillings, and enough gravy to drown a small car. Our steak and ale is the one that sells out first, but the chicken, leek, and tarragon is a dark horse — delicate, creamy, the kind of thing that makes people go quiet while they eat. For events we bring a proper pie bar: guests choose their filling, we slice and plate with creamy mash, mushy peas, and gravy from a giant pot. It works at weddings (surprisingly elegant with the right presentation), bonfire night parties (obviously), and any event where you want people to feel looked after.
pricing_notes: £10-14 per head for pie, mash, and sides. Minimum spend £350. Mini pies for canapé service £4 each.
setup_requirements: Kitchen access or 2x 13amp sockets for warming. Can do outdoor with gazebo. Need serving table.
peak_season: October to March — but pie has no season really
signature_items: Steak & ale pie with suet crust
founder_story: Former pastry chef Gareth wanted to prove that pies can be fine dining. He's been proving it at weddings and wakes for eight years now.
reviews_sample: We had pie and mash at our November wedding and it was PERFECT. Guests loved it. — Beth, wedding
Dad's favourite food is pie. This was the obvious choice for his 70th. He cried. — Sam, 70th birthday
Mini pies as canapés were a genius move. Everyone wanted the steak and ale one. — Hannah, corporate event
booking_notes: Mini pies work brilliantly as canapés alongside another main caterer. Can do bespoke fillings for weddings. Treacle tart is the dessert to book — it goes fast.

name: Sugar Rush
short_description: Hot donuts, churros, and crêpes from a candy-striped van. The sweet ending your event deserves.
long_description: We're the dessert course that shows up in a van. Sugar Rush has been making people's events sweeter since 2019 — literally. Our donuts are fried to order (watch them puff up through the glass), tossed in cinnamon sugar, and filled with salted caramel, Nutella, or lemon curd right in front of you. The churros come with three dipping sauces, and our crêpes are so thin you can nearly see through them. The van is candy-striped pink and white, covered in fairy lights, and smells like a bakery having a party. We're the add-on that steals the show.
pricing_notes: From £350 for 2 hours. £5-7 per head for unlimited donuts/churros. Crêpe station from £6 per head.
setup_requirements: Vehicle access, flat ground. Self-contained. Outdoor or large indoor space with ventilation.
peak_season: Year-round — summer for outdoor events, winter for markets and festive parties
signature_items: Churros with chocolate, caramel & strawberry dips
reviews_sample: The kids went absolutely feral for the donuts. Best thing we booked for the school fair. — Paul, school fête
Late-night churros at our wedding were the move. Everyone abandoned the dance floor. — Kim, wedding
The van is SO cute. Perfect for photos. And the crêpes are delicious. — Jess, baby shower
booking_notes: Pairs perfectly with a main food vendor — we're the dessert course. Can do 'donut wall' displays for weddings. Vegan options available.

name: Negroni Express
short_description: Mobile cocktail bar in a converted Citroën H van. Proper drinks, proper bartenders.
long_description: We converted a 1966 Citroën H van into a cocktail bar because putting a bar on wheels felt like the most useful thing anyone's ever done with a van. Our bartenders are ex-Callooh Callay and Happiness Forgets — people who actually know how to make a drink and hold a conversation while they do it. We build bespoke cocktail menus for each event (you pick 3-4 serves, we design them around your theme), and we bring everything: the bar, the ice, the glassware, the garnishes. We also do espresso martini stations, gin bars, and a very popular 'Negroni on tap' setup that has genuinely changed people's opinion of this drink.
pricing_notes: From £800 for 3 hours with 2 bartenders. £12-18 per head for unlimited cocktails. Cash/card bar option available.
setup_requirements: Vehicle access. Flat ground for the van. Power not essential but helpful for ice machine. Outdoor or large venues.
peak_season: May to September for outdoor events, December for Christmas parties
founder_story: Built by two bartenders who got tired of working behind other people's bars and wanted to bring theirs to the party.
reviews_sample: The van looked stunning at our wedding. The espresso martinis were flowing and nobody wanted to leave. — Fiona, wedding
Best cocktails I've had at a corporate event. The bespoke menu matched our brand colours, which was a nice touch. — Greg, corporate
The Negroni on tap is dangerously good. We've already rebooked for next year. — Nick, 50th birthday
booking_notes: Bespoke menu consultation included for weddings. Non-alcoholic cocktail menu always available. Can provide branded cup sleeves/napkins for corporate. Licensed — we handle all paperwork.

name: Drop & Graze
short_description: Drop-off canapés and grazing boxes delivered to your door. Beautiful food, zero faff.
long_description: We make the food and bring it to you. No van, no setup, no staff hanging around — just restaurant-quality canapés and platters delivered to your kitchen, ready to plate or already plated. Our range runs from classic (smoked salmon blinis, mini beef wellingtons) to modern (miso aubergine bites, prawn toast with yuzu mayo), and everything arrives in beautiful packaging that's ready to go straight to the table. We started during lockdown when everyone was hosting at home, and we stuck around because honestly, sometimes you just want the food without the circus.
pricing_notes: From £12 per head for canapé selection (6 pieces). Grazing boxes from £18 per head. Free delivery within 5 miles, £15 beyond.
setup_requirements: None — we deliver to your door. Just need a fridge if ordering more than 2 hours before serving.
peak_season: Christmas party season and summer garden parties
signature_items: Smoked salmon blinis with crème fraîche & dill
Grazing box for 10 (charcuterie, cheese, crackers, fruit)
founder_story: Started by former Ottolenghi chef Maya during lockdown. What began as a side project now does 30+ deliveries a week.
reviews_sample: Ordered for a dinner party — everything arrived looking like a magazine shoot. Tasted even better. — Clare, dinner party
The grazing boxes are our go-to for office meetings now. Always impressive. — Pete, corporate
Perfect for a small christening. No stress, just beautiful food. — Anna, christening
booking_notes: Minimum order £200. Can do next-day delivery for most items. Custom menus for events over £500. Everything arrives in compostable packaging.

name: Holy Smoke Pizza
short_description: Neapolitan pizza fired in 90 seconds from a converted Land Rover. Yes, really.
long_description: We bolted an Alfa Forni oven to the back of a 1983 Land Rover Defender and somehow it's the best business decision anyone's ever made. The pizzas are proper Neapolitan — high-hydration dough, San Marzano tomatoes, fior di latte — cooked in 90 seconds at 450°C. The Defender (Moses) is army green and looks absurdly cool parked in a field or a pub car park. We do 60-80 pizzas an hour at full tilt, which means your queue is never longer than a few minutes. We keep the menu tight: five pizzas, one special, one dessert. No decision fatigue, just great food and a Land Rover with a chimney.
pricing_notes: £13-16 per head for unlimited pizza. Minimum spend £650. Includes salad and dough balls to start.
setup_requirements: Vehicle access for Land Rover. Flat outdoor space 4m x 4m. Self-contained — we bring wood and gas backup.
peak_season: May to September — Moses likes the sunshine
signature_items: Classic Margherita (San Marzano, fior di latte, basil)
Spicy soppressata with Calabrian chilli honey
Vegan garden pizza (seasonal vegetables, cashew cream)
Garlic dough balls with rosemary oil
founder_story: Tom was a geography teacher who spent every holiday in Naples eating pizza. He bought the Land Rover on a whim and the oven on even less of one.
reviews_sample: Moses the Land Rover was the star of our wedding. The pizza was insane. — Gemma, wedding
80 pizzas in an hour. Not a single complaint. Just happy, cheese-faced people. — Rob, 30th birthday
Kids could watch the pizzas being made — they were transfixed. And the food was brilliant. — Liz, school fête
booking_notes: Moses is very Instagrammable — great for wedding photos. Gluten-free bases available (not coeliac safe due to shared oven). Tastings for weddings.

name: Smoke & Barrel
short_description: Southern US-style BBQ with London swagger. Pulled pork, ribs, and brisket done right.
long_description: We've got two smokers, a trailer full of cherry and oak wood, and an unhealthy obsession with internal meat temperatures. Smoke & Barrel is proper American BBQ — we're talking 12-hour brisket with a bark so dark it looks burnt (it's not), St Louis ribs with a bourbon glaze, and pulled pork that falls apart if you look at it sternly. We don't do fusion or twists or reimaginations. We just do the classics, executed perfectly, in large quantities. We've done festivals, pub takeovers, and about 100 weddings where the groom chose the caterer. Our coleslaw is made fresh, our cornbread has actual corn in it, and our mac and cheese has three types of cheese because two isn't enough.
pricing_notes: £15-22 per head for meat, two sides, and cornbread. Minimum spend £900. Ribs as add-on £5 per head.
setup_requirements: Outdoor space 6m x 4m for smoker setup. No power needed. We bring everything including disposable plates and cutlery.
peak_season: Summer BBQ season, but winter weddings in barns are surprisingly popular
signature_items: St Louis ribs with bourbon glaze
Pulled pork with house BBQ sauce
reviews_sample: The brisket. THE BRISKET. I'm a Texan and this is the real deal. — Mike, wedding
Fed 200 people at our summer party. Not a scrap left. — Jenna, corporate event
My husband chose the BBQ caterer for our wedding and for once he nailed it. — Chloe, wedding
booking_notes: Vegetarian sides available but we're a meat-focused operation — if you need strong veggie options, consider pairing us with a veggie vendor. Can do late-night pulled pork rolls.

name: Green Machine
short_description: 100% plant-based street food that even meat-eaters fight over. No compromise, all flavour.
long_description: We're the vegan vendor that carnivores actually want to eat from. Green Machine started at Chatsworth Road Market with a single dish — our smoked jackfruit 'pulled pork' burger — and people went so mental for it that we built a truck. Everything is made from scratch and entirely plant-based: our burgers use a house-blend patty (beetroot, black bean, smoked paprika), the 'chicken' is seitan marinated in buttermilk (oat, obviously), and our loaded fries come with cashew cheese sauce that's cracked the code. We don't do sad salads or apologetic tofu. We do food that happens to be vegan and happens to be outstanding.
pricing_notes: £10-14 per head. Minimum spend £450. Corporate lunch packages from £12 per head with sides.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m space. One 13amp socket. Can do indoor or outdoor. We bring our own grill and prep station.
peak_season: Veganuary (January) and summer festival season
signature_items: Seitan 'chicken' burger with hot sauce & slaw
Loaded fries with cashew cheese sauce
founder_story: Chef Jade went vegan in 2019 and got frustrated that 'vegan street food' meant a falafel wrap. So she started cooking what she actually wanted to eat.
reviews_sample: I'm not vegan and I'm obsessed with this food. The jackfruit burger is ridiculous. — Tom, festival
Perfect for our mixed office — everyone ate well, nobody felt left out. — Sarah, corporate lunch
Our wedding was half-vegan, half-not. Green Machine kept everyone happy. — Ash, wedding
booking_notes: 100% plant-based kitchen — zero cross-contamination. Can cater alongside a non-vegan vendor without issues. Compostable packaging as standard.

name: Neighbourhood Pizza
short_description: Wood-fired pizza from a mint-green Piaggio Ape. Small van, big flavour, maximum charm.
long_description: We're a tiny Piaggio Ape with an oven strapped to the back and more charm than should be legally allowed. Neighbourhood Pizza does intimate events — we're not here to feed 300, we're here to make your garden party or intimate wedding feel like a night out in Rome. Our dough is slow-fermented for 72 hours (we're patient people), and we top it with the best ingredients we can find: burrata from La Latteria, nduja from Natoora, and whatever's beautiful at the market that morning. The Ape (called Valentina) fits through gates, down alleys, and into back gardens that bigger vans can't reach.
pricing_notes: £15-20 per head. Minimum spend £500. Maximum 80 guests due to oven size. Premium ingredients reflected in price.
setup_requirements: Access for small three-wheeler vehicle. 3m x 2m space. Outdoor only. Self-contained.
peak_season: May to September
founder_story: Valentina the Ape was bought on a family holiday in Sicily. The oven was added in a garage in Stamford Hill. The rest is history.
reviews_sample: The Piaggio is SO charming. Our guests couldn't stop taking photos. And the burrata pizza was divine. — Lisa, garden party
Perfect for our small wedding — only 35 guests, and it felt personal and special. — Matt, wedding
booking_notes: Best for smaller, intimate events. Can't do more than 80 guests due to oven capacity. Book early for summer — we only take one event per weekend day.

name: Otis Burgers
short_description: Premium burgers from a former Michelin-kitchen chef. The smash burger, elevated.
long_description: Otis is what happens when a Michelin-trained chef decides he'd rather cook burgers. Our patties are a custom blend from The Butchery in Bermondsey — 30-day aged chuck and short rib — smashed thin on a scorching plancha, finished with American cheese, house pickles, and a sauce that took 47 attempts to perfect. The bun is a brioche collaboration with a bakery in Dalston. Everything about this burger is considered, but nothing about it is pretentious — it's still a burger, it's still messy, and it's still best eaten slightly drunk at 10pm. We also do a fried chicken number and a halloumi option that's honestly no compromise.
pricing_notes: £12-16 per head for burger, fries, and slaw. Minimum spend £600. Late-night slider menu available.
setup_requirements: 5m x 3m for the truck. Outdoor only. Self-contained. Can do late-night with lighting.
peak_season: Summer, but we love a winter wedding with burgers by the fire pit
signature_items: The Otis (double smash, American cheese, house pickles, Otis sauce)
Fried chicken burger with hot honey & slaw
founder_story: Head chef Otis left a two-star kitchen in Mayfair because he wanted to cook food people actually eat on a Saturday night.
reviews_sample: Best burger I've ever had. At a wedding. In a field. At midnight. It was perfect. — Claire, wedding
The truffle fries are worth the booking alone. Food was exceptional. — Dan, 40th birthday
Hired for a product launch — the food matched the brand perfectly. Premium but fun. — Anya, corporate event
booking_notes: Late-night slider service (10pm-midnight) is hugely popular for weddings. Tasting sessions for events over £1.5k.

name: Chai & Naan
short_description: Fresh naan from a tandoor oven, loaded curries, and masala chai on tap. Proper Indian, no shortcuts.
long_description: We bring a tandoor oven to your event and bake naan to order. That sentence alone has booked us 200+ events. There's something hypnotic about watching bread slapped against the inside of a clay oven, puffing up in seconds, coming out charred and buttery. We pair it with slow-cooked curries — our butter chicken has a 6-hour tomato base, the lamb rogan josh uses shoulder braised until it surrenders, and the chana masala is so good our vegetarian clients don't feel like they're missing out. The chai comes from a proper brass urn, brewed with cardamom, ginger, and real tea leaves. It's the closer.
pricing_notes: £14-20 per head for curry, naan, rice, sides. Minimum spend £700. Chai station £3 per head. Tandoor is always included.
setup_requirements: 6m x 3m outdoor space for tandoor and serving. Power not essential. Outdoor or very well-ventilated indoor space.
peak_season: Wedding season (May-Sep) and Diwali/Christmas
signature_items: Masala chai from a brass urn
founder_story: Raj's family has been catering weddings in Southall for 30 years. He modernised the setup for the festival/outdoor event market.
reviews_sample: The tandoor naan was the moment of our wedding. People were crowded around watching. Incredible food. — Priti, wedding
Fed 200 people at our Diwali party. Everything was perfect, nothing ran out. — Amit, private party
Our multicultural wedding needed Indian food that would wow everyone. Chai & Naan delivered. — Sarah, wedding
booking_notes: Halal certified. Tandoor is always brought — it's non-negotiable, that's our thing. Can handle events up to 300. Tasting for bookings over £1.5k.

name: Wheels of Cheese
short_description: Fondue, raclette, and cheese boards from a cheese-obsessed duo. Melting things since 2020.
long_description: We're a mobile cheese operation. Our main thing is the raclette setup — a massive half-wheel of Swiss raclette under the grill, scraped bubbling and golden over new potatoes, cornichons, and charcuterie. It's interactive, it's theatrical, and it smells incredible. We also do fondue pots (classic, truffle, or blue cheese), cheese boards with notes on every cheese, and a mac & cheese bar where guests choose their own mix-ins. Everything comes from Neal's Yard Dairy, The Cheese Truck's supplier, or directly from cheesemakers we visit in the Alps every year (yes, it's a tough life). We are cheesemongers first, caterers second.
pricing_notes: Raclette station from £400 (up to 40 portions). Fondue from £15 per head. Full cheese table from £25 per head.
setup_requirements: Table for setup, one 13amp socket for raclette grill. Indoor or covered outdoor. We bring all equipment and serving ware.
peak_season: October to March for raclette (it's a cold weather thing), year-round for cheese boards
signature_items: Curated cheese board with tasting notes
Mac & cheese bar (choose your own cheeses)
founder_story: Best friends Jo and Marcus bonded over a shared conviction that melted cheese is the highest form of food.
reviews_sample: The raclette was the most popular thing at our winter wedding. People were queueing in the cold for it. — Emma, wedding
A fondue station at our anniversary dinner — romantic, fun, and absolutely delicious. — Paul, anniversary
The cheese board had tasting notes for every single cheese. So thoughtful. — Leah, baby shower
booking_notes: Raclette works best as a starter or evening food alongside a main caterer. We can do standalone for smaller events. All cheese is sourced from British and Alpine producers.

name: Masa & Madre
short_description: Baja-style fish tacos and mezcal margaritas. A little bit of Tulum in your garden.
long_description: We do fish tacos. Really, really well. Beer-battered cod on a warm corn tortilla with pickled red onion, chipotle crema, and a squeeze of lime. It's the dish that built our reputation at markets across east London, and it's the dish that books us 50+ weddings a year. But we're not a one-trick pony — the birria tacos (slow-braised beef shin, dipped in consommé) are the sleeper hit, and the grilled prawn tacos with mango salsa are summer on a plate. We also run a mezcal margarita bar that's got us into serious trouble at several events. The truck is tiled in traditional Mexican Talavera patterns, and we play a playlist that goes from Selena to Bad Bunny.
pricing_notes: £12-16 per head for 3 tacos and sides. Minimum spend £550. Margarita bar add-on from £8 per head.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m for the truck. Self-contained. Outdoor or covered area. We bring our own lighting.
peak_season: Summer, especially July and August
signature_items: Baja fish tacos (beer-battered cod, chipotle crema)
reviews_sample: The fish tacos are a religious experience. Booked them for our wedding and we'd do it again tomorrow. — Freya, wedding
The birria tacos were a surprise hit — everyone was dipping and making a beautiful mess. — Jack, 30th birthday
Mezcal margaritas at a corporate summer party. HR approved (barely). — Tara, corporate event
booking_notes: Fish tacos are our signature — always recommend including them. Mezcal margarita bar requires TEN licence (we can help with paperwork). Veggie options on request.

name: Rolling Scones
short_description: Cream tea service from a vintage Citroën van. Scones, clotted cream, and everything proper.
long_description: We do cream teas. From a van. And before you say 'how hard can that be', try baking 200 scones at 4am and getting them to a field in Hampshire while they're still warm. Our scones are the real thing — buttermilk, cold butter, a light hand — and they come with Rodda's clotted cream and house-made strawberry jam. We serve on vintage china (yes, actual china — we wash it ourselves afterwards), with a tiered cake stand and a pot of proper loose-leaf tea. It's absurdly British, completely charming, and works at weddings, garden parties, hen dos, and any event where you want to feel like you're in a Sunday BBC drama.
pricing_notes: £12-16 per head for full cream tea (2 scones, cream, jam, tea). Minimum spend £350. Prosecco upgrade £5 per head.
setup_requirements: Access for Citroën van. Flat area 3m x 2m. Self-contained. Outdoor preferred but can do indoor.
peak_season: May to September — garden party season
signature_items: Buttermilk scones with clotted cream & jam
founder_story: Former Great British Bake Off applicant (didn't get on, still bitter, makes better scones than anyone who did).
reviews_sample: The vintage china, the tiered stands, the warm scones — it was like stepping into a period drama. Guests loved it. — Alice, wedding
Perfect hen do activity. Prosecco and scones in the garden. Everyone was happy. — Vicky, hen party
My nan said they were the best scones she'd had since 1974. That's the highest compliment possible. — Josh, christening
booking_notes: All served on real vintage china — we bring enough for your guest count. Prosecco afternoon tea is our most popular wedding package. Gluten-free scones available with 48hr notice.

name: Pandan Club
primary_category: bao, dumplings, and Asian street food
short_description: Southeast Asian street food with a London edge. Satay, roti, and pandan cake that slaps.
long_description: Pandan Club is what happens when Malaysian, Singaporean, and Indonesian street food meets London's event scene. We do char kway teow (smoky flat noodles tossed in a screaming hot wok), chicken satay with a peanut sauce that's got actual complexity (not just peanut butter and soy), and roti canai that's pulled and flipped to order — stretchy, flaky, and best dunked in our house curry sauce. The dessert situation is serious: pandan layer cake, kaya toast, and coconut ice cream with gula melaka. We're run by Jess, whose parents ran a hawker stall in Penang, and you can taste the lineage in everything we make.
pricing_notes: £12-16 per head for main + side. Minimum spend £550. Roti station add-on £4 per head. Desserts £5 per head.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m space. Two 13amp sockets for wok burner and roti griddle. Indoor or outdoor with extraction.
peak_season: Year-round — noodles don't have a season
signature_items: Chicken satay with house peanut sauce
Roti canai pulled to order with curry sauce
Coconut ice cream with gula melaka
founder_story: Jess's parents ran a hawker stall in Penang for 25 years. She learned to pull roti before she could ride a bike.
reviews_sample: The roti station was mesmerising. Watching Jess flip the dough is a performance. And it tastes incredible. — Nina, 30th birthday
Best corporate event food we've ever had. Everyone wanted seconds of the satay. — Ben, corporate event
The pandan cake is a revelation. I've been thinking about it for weeks. — Maya, private party
booking_notes: Roti station is highly recommended — it's interactive and guests love watching. Halal menu available. Pandan cake can be ordered separately as a birthday cake alternative.

name: Brûlée
short_description: French-style crêpes and crème brûlée torched to order. A little Paris in your postcode.
long_description: We make crêpes the way they should be made — thin, lacy, slightly crispy at the edges — on a traditional French billig (a cast-iron crêpe griddle that weighs more than our van). Fillings run from classic (lemon & sugar, Nutella & banana) to signature (salted caramel & pecan, dark chocolate & sea salt), and every crêpe is folded and served in under two minutes. But the thing that gets the most attention is the crème brûlée: we make them in individual ramekins, then torch the sugar in front of your guests. That crack when you break through the caramelised top? That's the sound of a successful event.
pricing_notes: £5-8 per head for crêpes. Crème brûlée from £4 each. Minimum spend £300. Can combine both for a dessert package.
setup_requirements: 2m x 2m space. One 13amp socket for the billig. Indoor or outdoor. We bring everything including the blowtorch.
peak_season: Year-round — works at summer garden parties and winter markets equally
reviews_sample: Watching the crème brûlée being torched was the highlight of the party. Kids AND adults loved it. — Jo, school fête
Late-night crêpes at our wedding. Simple, delicious, and exactly what everyone wanted at 11pm. — Rosie, wedding
The salted caramel crêpe should be illegal. We've already rebooked. — Sam, birthday party
booking_notes: Crème brûlée torching is very popular for evening events — the flame in the dark is very photogenic. Pairs well with a main food vendor. Can do a combined crêpe + coffee setup.

name: Yalla Wraps
short_description: Shawarma carved from the spit, house-made hummus, and flatbreads off the grill. No shortcuts.
long_description: The vertical spit is the centrepiece of everything we do. We marinate chicken for 48 hours in a seven-spice blend, stack it on the spit in our truck, and carve it to order while it's still sizzling. It goes in a grilled flatbread with our garlic toum (the recipe hasn't changed in three generations), pickled turnips, and a drizzle of chilli oil. The hummus is made fresh every morning — Natoora chickpeas, tahini from Belazu, a silly amount of lemon — and it's smoother than anything you'll find in a supermarket. We serve it warm, which is how it's meant to be eaten. We're fast, we're loud, and we've never had a complaint about portions.
pricing_notes: £8-12 per head for wrap or plate. Minimum spend £450. Mezze platter starter add-on £5 per head.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m for the truck. Self-contained with gas. Outdoor or covered. We bring our own spit and grill.
peak_season: Year-round — wraps work in any weather
signature_items: Warm hummus with olive oil & paprika
founder_story: Hassan grew up watching his uncle carve shawarma at a shop on Green Lanes. He's been doing the same thing from a truck since 2019.
reviews_sample: The shawarma is the real deal. Guests were queuing and nobody minded. Portions are huge. — Omar, wedding
Affordable, delicious, halal. Exactly what we needed for Eid. — Fatima, private party
Fed 120 people at our summer BBQ. Nobody went hungry, and the hummus disappeared in minutes. — Steve, corporate event
booking_notes: Halal certified. Can feed large numbers quickly — we've done 250 in under 2 hours. Mezze platters work well as starters before the main shawarma service.

name: Buttercream Dreams
secondary_categories: ice cream vans and gelato carts
short_description: Custom celebration cakes and a dessert table that'll ruin your diet. Beautifully.
long_description: We make celebration cakes that make people gasp, and dessert tables that make them groan with happiness. Every cake is bespoke — we do consultations where we taste, sketch, and obsess over every detail until it's exactly what you want. Our signature is the 'naked cake' with fresh flowers and seasonal fruit, but we've done everything from a 5-tier ombré for a Shoreditch wedding to a realistic-looking pizza cake for a toddler (his face was priceless). The dessert table is where we really go to town: mini éclairs, macarons, brownies, lemon tarts, cake pops, and whatever else we're obsessed with that month.
pricing_notes: Celebration cakes from £250. Dessert tables from £15 per head (min 30 guests). Delivery included within 10 miles.
setup_requirements: Table for dessert display. Fridge access for cakes (or we deliver as close to serving time as possible). Indoor preferred.
peak_season: Wedding season (May-Sep) and Christmas
signature_items: Naked cake with fresh flowers & seasonal fruit
founder_story: Pastry chef Ellie left Ottolenghi to start baking from her kitchen in Walthamstow. Six years later she has a team of four and a studio that smells permanently of butter.
reviews_sample: Our wedding cake was the most beautiful thing at the entire wedding (sorry, husband). — Jess, wedding
The dessert table was a work of art. Guests were taking photos before they ate anything. — Mike, 50th birthday
Ellie made a vegan cake that nobody believed was vegan. That's the highest compliment. — Tanya, anniversary
booking_notes: Free tasting consultation for wedding cakes. Dessert tables can be styled to match your event theme/colours. Delivery and setup included for events over £500.

name: Flat Iron Social
short_description: Speciality coffee and espresso martinis from a timber-clad cart. Morning fuel and evening trouble.
long_description: We do two things: morning coffee that's better than whatever's in your kitchen cupboard, and evening espresso martinis that make people miss their Uber home. Our cart is built from reclaimed timber with brass fittings, and it fits into venues that a van can't reach — courtyards, atriums, rooftops, the weird bit at the back of your venue where nothing else goes. We use rotating single-origin espresso from Square Mile, pull on a Slayer, and our baristas do latte art that actually looks like something. For evening events, the espresso martini setup is slick: batch-made for speed, shaken for theatre, and served with a coffee bean that's not just decorative.
pricing_notes: Coffee service from £450 for 2 hours. Espresso martini bar from £12 per head. Combined day-to-night packages available.
setup_requirements: 1.5m x 1m for the cart. One 13amp socket. Indoor or outdoor. We bring filtered water.
peak_season: Wedding season and corporate Q4
signature_items: Oat milk flat white with latte art
reviews_sample: Best coffee at any wedding I've been to. The latte art was a lovely touch. — Lily, wedding
Espresso martini station at our Christmas party. Nobody wanted to leave. — Dan, corporate event
booking_notes: Cart fits through standard doorways. Day-to-night packages (coffee in the afternoon, espresso martinis in the evening) are our bestseller. Custom branded cups for corporate.

name: The Pizza Pilgrims Van
short_description: Frying pan pizza, Margherita masterclass, and all the joy of Naples in a van.
long_description: We've done the pilgrimage (literally — our founders drove a three-wheeler from London to Naples in 2012), and we've brought back everything we learned. Our van runs a Stefano Ferrara oven imported from Naples, and our pizzaiolo trained at L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele. But we're not precious about it — pizza is fun food, and our events feel like a party, not a tasting menu. We do frying pan pizza workshops where guests make their own (messier than you'd think, funnier than you'd expect), alongside our regular service of Margheritas, nduja, and a daily special. We pair well with a few Peroni, good music, and people who are hungry.
pricing_notes: £13-17 per head for unlimited pizza. Minimum spend £700. Frying pan workshop add-on £8 per head.
setup_requirements: Vehicle access, 5m x 4m outdoor space. Self-contained. Outdoor only.
peak_season: May to September
signature_items: Margherita (San Marzano, fior di latte, basil)
founder_story: Two brothers drove a Piaggio from London to Naples, learned to make pizza, and drove back. The van came later.
reviews_sample: The frying pan workshop was the best team-building activity we've ever done. And the pizza was brilliant. — Martin, corporate event
Fed 200 guests at our wedding without breaking a sweat. The Nutella calzone at midnight was genius. — Kate, wedding
Kids made their own pizzas and ate them. Zero waste, maximum joy. — Hannah, birthday party
booking_notes: Frying pan pizza workshops are brilliant for corporate team-building. We've catered events for 300+ with two ovens. Book 4-6 weeks ahead for summer weekends.

name: Smoke & Bones
short_description: Whole-hog BBQ and bone marrow burgers. Not for the faint-hearted. Or the vegetarian.
long_description: We do nose-to-tail BBQ. Our whole hog — butterflied, rubbed with fennel and chilli, smoked for 16 hours — is the centrepiece, and it's as theatrical as food gets. We also do beef short ribs, lamb shoulders, and our signature bone marrow burger (the patty is mixed with roasted bone marrow, which sounds mad but tastes like the best thing you've ever eaten). We're based in an arch in Bermondsey where we prep and smoke everything before loading onto the trailer. We're not for everyone — our food is rich, unapologetic, and very much meat — but for the right event, there's nothing like it.
pricing_notes: Whole hog from £1,500 (feeds 80-100). Per head pricing £20-30 for mixed BBQ menu. Minimum spend £1,500.
setup_requirements: Large outdoor space 8m x 5m. Self-contained. Not suitable for indoor events. Early access needed (we arrive 6+ hours before service).
peak_season: Summer BBQ season (May-September)
signature_items: Beef short ribs with coffee rub
founder_story: Former butcher Marcus spent a year travelling the American South, eating at every BBQ joint he could find, then came home and built a smoker.
reviews_sample: The whole hog was the talking point of our wedding. Guests still bring it up a year later. — Tom, wedding
The bone marrow burger changed my life. I'm not being dramatic. — Phil, festival
They fed 150 people and everyone was groaning with happiness. Portions are enormous. — Ruth, 50th birthday
booking_notes: The whole hog is our showpiece — highly recommend for weddings. We need early access (6am for evening service). Can pair with a veggie vendor for mixed dietary events.

name: Momo Mama
primary_category: bao, dumplings, and Asian street food
short_description: Nepali momos steamed and fried to order. Spicy tomato achar on everything.
long_description: Momos are Nepal's gift to the world and we're here to spread the gospel. Our dumplings are hand-pleated (25 pleats per momo — yes, we count), filled with spiced chicken, pork, or vegetables, and served steamed or fried with our fiery tomato achar that's made from a recipe Sita's grandmother brought from Kathmandu. For events, we set up a steaming station with towers of bamboo baskets — the steam, the smell, the drama of lifting the lid — it's street food theatre at its best. We also do thukpa (Nepali noodle soup) for winter events and a pan-fried momo that's crispy on the bottom and juicy on top.
pricing_notes: £8-12 per head for 6-8 momos with sides. Minimum spend £400. Thukpa soup add-on £4 per head.
setup_requirements: 3m x 2m space. One 13amp socket for steamer. Indoor or outdoor. We bring bamboo steamers and all equipment.
peak_season: Year-round — momos work in any season
signature_items: Steamed chicken momos with tomato achar
Vegetable momos with spiced potato & cabbage
Jhol momo (momos in spicy sesame soup)
founder_story: Sita came to London from Kathmandu at 19 and missed her grandmother's momos so much she started making them for everyone.
reviews_sample: The momos are addictive. I ate 12 and regret nothing. The achar sauce is incredible. — Alex, birthday party
Best value event food we've found. Fed 60 people for under £500 and everyone was full and happy. — Jen, corporate lunch
The steamer towers look amazing. Great for photos and even better for eating. — Tom, festival
booking_notes: Momos are great as canapés (3 per person) or as a main (6-8 per person). The pan-fried version is our most popular for events. Can do gluten-free wrappers on request.

name: Tongue & Cheek
short_description: Cheek burgers, beef tongue tacos, and offal-forward street food for the adventurous eater.
long_description: We cook the bits other people throw away, and we make them taste incredible. Our signature is the ox cheek burger — braised for 8 hours, shredded, pressed, then griddled until crispy on the outside and melting inside. It's served on a pretzel bun with bone marrow butter and gherkin relish. We also do beef tongue tacos (sliced thin, chargrilled, with salsa verde) and a devilled kidney number that's divided opinion at every event we've ever done. We're not for everyone and we know it — but if you want food that people will actually talk about, not just eat and forget, we're your lot.
pricing_notes: £12-16 per head. Minimum spend £500. Tasting menu format available for smaller events.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m for the truck. Outdoor or well-ventilated indoor. Self-contained.
peak_season: Year-round — we thrive on the weird and wonderful
signature_items: 8-hour braised ox cheek burger on pretzel bun
Beef tongue tacos with salsa verde
founder_story: Ex-St. John sous chef who believes the offal cuts are the best cuts and wants to prove it to everyone.
reviews_sample: The ox cheek burger is a masterpiece. I've been boring everyone about it for weeks. — Clara, 40th birthday
Definitely not for everyone, but our guests loved the surprise factor. Great conversation starter. — Pete, private party
booking_notes: We always include 'safe' options alongside the adventurous stuff. Happy to design a menu that eases guests in. Tasting sessions highly recommended.

name: Dosa Deli
short_description: South Indian dosas cooked on a massive tawa. Crispy, golden, filled with whatever you fancy.
long_description: We've got a 4-foot tawa and we're not afraid to use it. Our dosas are made from a rice and urad dal batter that's fermented for 24 hours — it's the fermentation that gives them that slight tang and that incredible crispiness. We spread the batter thin on the tawa, fill it with spiced potato masala, fold it, and serve it with coconut chutney and sambar. But we've also got modern fillings: paneer & spinach, spiced lamb keema, and a roasted cauliflower & cashew number that vegans go absolutely wild for. The whole setup is interactive — guests watch the dosa being made, hear it sizzle, and smell it from across the room.
pricing_notes: £8-12 per head. Minimum spend £450. Chai and lassi add-ons available. South Indian thali option for sit-down events.
setup_requirements: 3m x 2m space for the tawa station. One 13amp socket. Indoor or outdoor (outdoor preferred for the theatre). We bring everything.
peak_season: Year-round
signature_items: Classic masala dosa with potato filling
founder_story: Kavitha learned to make dosa from her mother in Chennai. She makes 200+ a day during busy weekends and still finds it meditative.
reviews_sample: Watching the dosas being made was mesmerising. And they taste as good as they look. — Ruth, private party
Best corporate event food decision we ever made. Everyone ate well, including our vegan colleagues. — Amit, corporate event
The lamb keema dosa is extraordinary. We're already planning when to book again. — Simon, 50th birthday
booking_notes: The tawa is the showpiece — always recommend placing it where guests can watch. Entirely vegetarian batter (rice & lentil) so safe for all dietary requirements. Can combine with our chai station.

name: Goodness Gracious
short_description: Plant-based catering that looks like a magazine and tastes like someone actually cares.
long_description: We're a fully plant-based catering company that refuses to be boring. Our food is built on Middle Eastern and Mediterranean flavours — roasted cauliflower with zhug and tahini, wild mushroom & walnut kofta, a beetroot & blackberry salad that's so beautiful it hurts to eat it. We do plated dinners for intimate weddings, sharing tables for garden parties, and grazing boards that prove cheese isn't the only thing worth putting on a board. Our founder Lucy is a former food photographer, which is why everything looks obscenely good — but it's the flavour that brings people back. We've catered for carnivores who didn't notice there was no meat until we told them.
pricing_notes: £20-30 per head for sharing menu. Plated dinner from £35 per head. Minimum spend £500. Includes service staff.
setup_requirements: Kitchen access for plated service. For sharing/grazing, just need table space. Indoor preferred. We bring serving ware and staff.
peak_season: Wedding season and Veganuary
signature_items: Whole roasted cauliflower with zhug & tahini
Beetroot & blackberry salad with pistachio dukkah
Olive oil cake with citrus & rosemary
founder_story: Lucy was a food photographer who went vegan and got frustrated that 'vegan catering' meant a sad salad and some hummus. She started cooking the food she wanted to photograph.
reviews_sample: Our wedding was fully vegan and NOBODY noticed until the speeches. That's how good the food was. — Nell, wedding
The cauliflower is a showstopper. It arrived whole and everyone crowded around to watch it being carved. — James, private party
Every dish looked like a magazine cover. Tasted even better. — Priya, baby shower
booking_notes: Tasting dinner for wedding clients (£75 for two, redeemable against booking). Can work alongside a non-vegan caterer without issues. Service staff included in per-head pricing.

name: Souvlaki Street
short_description: Greek souvlaki, grilled halloumi, and loukoumades. Like a taverna on wheels.
long_description: We're a Greek street food truck that smells like a Mykonos back street. Our souvlaki is marinated in oregano, lemon, and garlic, chargrilled on skewers, and served in warm pita with tzatziki, tomato, red onion, and a scattering of paprika. The halloumi is grilled until it squeaks, the loukoumades (Greek donuts) come drenched in honey and cinnamon, and we've got a side of gigantes (giant beans in tomato sauce) that converts every non-bean-eater. The truck is painted Aegean blue and white, we play Greek music that nobody understands but everyone loves, and on a warm evening it genuinely feels like you've been transported somewhere better.
pricing_notes: £9-13 per head for souvlaki meal with sides. Minimum spend £450. Loukoumades dessert add-on £4 per head.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m for the truck. Self-contained. Outdoor or covered area.
peak_season: Summer — but Greek food works all year
reviews_sample: The souvlaki was incredible. Simple, fresh, and absolutely perfect for a summer party. — Maria, birthday party
Kids loved the chicken skewers. Adults loved the halloumi. Everyone loved the donuts. — Phil, school fête
Best Greek food outside of actual Greece. The gigantes are life-changing. — Nikos, private party
booking_notes: Loukoumades (hot donuts) are a guaranteed crowd-pleaser — always recommend adding them. We bring our own charcoal grill. Can do mezze platters as starters.

name: Scoops & Ladders
primary_category: ice cream vans and gelato carts
short_description: Artisan ice cream from a sky-blue Bedford van. Seasonal flavours, no stabilisers, no nonsense.
long_description: We make ice cream the old way — Jersey cream, free-range eggs, British sugar, and whatever's good at the market. Our flavours change with the seasons: blood orange in winter, Kentish strawberry in summer, and a year-round salted caramel that has a near-religious following. We don't use stabilisers or artificial colours — if the pistachio is green, it's because we used a lot of pistachios. The van (Barbara) is a 1969 Bedford CF in powder blue, and she draws a crowd wherever she parks. We do weddings, garden parties, and school fêtes — anywhere people want to feel like it's a sunny Saturday afternoon.
pricing_notes: From £400 for 2 hours (up to 100 scoops). Then £3.50 per scoop. Unlimited service for weddings from £7 per head.
setup_requirements: Vehicle access. Flat ground. Self-contained. Outdoor or large covered area.
peak_season: May to September
founder_story: Former dairy farmer's daughter who decided the world needed better ice cream and a nicer van.
reviews_sample: Barbara the van stole the show at our wedding. And the salted caramel is worth the booking alone. — Jenny, wedding
Kids at the school fête were obsessed. We ran out of strawberry twice. — Dave, school fête
booking_notes: Vegan sorbets always available. Custom flavours for weddings with 4 weeks notice. Barbara is very photogenic — couples love her.

name: Bun Intended
short_description: Smash burgers and loaded hot dogs from a red double-decker bus. Top deck is the dining room.
long_description: We bought a retired Routemaster, ripped out the seats upstairs, put in tables and fairy lights, and turned the bottom deck into a kitchen. Guests order downstairs, then eat upstairs with a view. The burgers are double-smashed on a flat-top, the hot dogs are snappy natural-casing frankfurters from a butcher in Smithfield, and the onion rings are beer-battered and unreasonably large. It's the most fun catering setup in London — the bus IS the venue, the restaurant, and the talking point. We drive to your event, park up, and suddenly you've got a double-decker diner in your car park.
pricing_notes: From £800 (includes bus hire). £12-15 per head for burger or hot dog meal. Seating for 30 on top deck.
setup_requirements: Bus-accessible road and flat parking area. We're 4.4m tall — check height restrictions. Self-contained with generator.
peak_season: Summer events and festivals
signature_items: Double smash burger with American cheese
All-American hot dog with mustard & sauerkraut
founder_story: Two mates bought a Routemaster off TfL, had zero plan, and somehow ended up running London's only double-decker burger restaurant.
reviews_sample: The BUS. The actual double-decker bus parked in our field. Everyone lost their minds. Food was great too. — Adam, wedding
My son's face when a red bus pulled into our garden for his birthday. Best money I've ever spent. — Claire, 8th birthday
booking_notes: The bus is the draw — it's a venue AND a caterer. Top deck seats 30 for dining. Need to check road access and height clearance before booking.

name: Seoul Food
primary_category: bao, dumplings, and Asian street food
short_description: Korean fried chicken, kimchi fries, and bulgogi rice bowls. K-pop not included (but negotiable).
long_description: We fry chicken better than your favourite takeaway and we're not sorry about it. Our KFC (Korean Fried Chicken) is double-fried for maximum crunch, then glazed in either gochujang honey (sweet, spicy, sticky) or soy garlic (savoury, moreish, gone in seconds). We serve it with pickled daikon, rice, and our house kimchi — fermented in our kitchen in Stratford for three weeks minimum. The bulgogi rice bowls are the sensible option, and the kimchi fries are the chaotic option. We've done corporate lunches, late-night wedding snacks, and one legendary 500-person festival where we got through 400kg of chicken.
pricing_notes: £11-15 per head for chicken meal with rice and sides. Minimum spend £600. Late-night snack menu from £8 per head.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m space. Need 2x 13amp sockets for fryers. Indoor or outdoor with extraction. We bring our own oil and filtration.
peak_season: Year-round — fried chicken has no off-season
founder_story: Hana grew up in her parents' Korean restaurant in New Malden and wanted to take the food out of the restaurant and into the streets.
reviews_sample: The fried chicken is dangerously good. We ordered for 80 and could've done with more. — Rich, corporate summer party
Late-night fried chicken at 11pm at our wedding. Best decision we made. — Nat, wedding
The kimchi fries are chaos and I love them. — Jo, festival
booking_notes: Late-night service until midnight. Kimchi is made in-house and we're proud of it. Can do vegetarian Korean options on request.

name: Flour Power
short_description: Sourdough pizza with a 96-hour ferment. Slow food, served fast.
long_description: Our dough takes four days. We're aware that's insane. But that 96-hour cold ferment gives it a flavour and digestibility that shorter ferments can't touch — slightly sour, beautifully blistered, and so light you can eat three slices without realising. We run a custom-built trailer with twin Moretti ovens, which means we can serve two pizzas every 90 seconds at full capacity. The toppings are seasonal and locally sourced: heritage tomatoes in summer, purple sprouting broccoli in spring, wild mushrooms in autumn. We keep it tight — six pizzas on the menu, one rotating special — because constraints make better pizza.
pricing_notes: £14-18 per head for unlimited pizza. Minimum spend £600. Premium toppings (burrata, truffle) priced separately.
setup_requirements: 5m x 3m for the trailer. Flat outdoor space. Self-contained with wood and gas. Outdoor only.
peak_season: April to October
signature_items: Garlic bread with rosemary & sea salt
founder_story: Former sourdough bread baker who realised pizza dough is basically the same thing but more fun.
reviews_sample: The lightest, most flavourful pizza I've ever had. The ferment makes a real difference. — Claire, wedding
Seasonal toppings were brilliant — the wild mushroom pizza in October was sublime. — Marcus, private party
booking_notes: 96-hour ferment means we need confirmed guest count 5 days before. Gluten-free bases available but made in same area as wheat. Tastings for weddings.

name: The Naanery
short_description: Stuffed naans the size of your head and curry by the bowl. Indian soul food.
long_description: We make naans. Big ones. Our signature keema naan is stuffed with spiced lamb mince, slapped on the side of a tandoor, and pulled out puffy, charred, and steaming. Tear it open and dip it in our house dal or butter chicken sauce. We also do a cheese & garlic naan that's essentially a meal in itself, and a vegan potato & pea naan that's the sleeper hit of every event. The curries are the supporting cast: rich, slow-cooked, and designed for dipping. We keep it simple and generous — no tiny portions, no pretension, just big flavours and bigger naans.
pricing_notes: £8-12 per head for stuffed naan and curry. Minimum spend £450. Chai and dessert add-ons available.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m for tandoor setup. Outdoor or very well-ventilated. Self-contained with gas.
peak_season: Year-round
founder_story: Ali's uncle ran a tandoori restaurant on Brick Lane for 30 years. The naan recipe is his, the business model is Ali's.
reviews_sample: The naans are ENORMOUS. Everyone was stuffed and happy. Great value. — Sophie, birthday party
Best Indian street food at any event I've been to. The butter chicken is incredible. — Dan, corporate event
booking_notes: Halal certified. Naans are made to order so there's a short wait — worth it. Can do mini naans as canapés for formal events.

name: The Cheese Bar Mobile
short_description: Grilled cheese sandwiches, fondue, and the best toastie you'll eat this decade.
long_description: We started as a cheese shop in Camden, then someone asked if we could do events, and now we spend most weekends making grilled cheese sandwiches from a van. But these aren't normal toasties — we use Comté on sourdough with truffle honey, or Montgomery's Cheddar with beer-braised onions, or a four-cheese melt that pulls like a mozzarella ad. We also do fondue stations and raclette, but the toasties are the thing that sells out. The van has a glass panel so guests can watch the cheese melt on the plancha, which is basically therapy.
pricing_notes: £8-12 per head for grilled cheese meal with soup/salad. Minimum spend £450. Fondue station add-on from £400.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m for the van. Self-contained. Outdoor or covered area.
peak_season: October to March for comfort food, but we're busy year-round
founder_story: Mathew ran a cheese shop, got asked to do a friend's wedding, brought a plancha and some sourdough, and accidentally started a second business.
reviews_sample: The Comté and truffle honey toastie should be classified as a controlled substance. — James, corporate event
Winter wedding + grilled cheese = genius. Our guests still talk about it. — Sara, wedding
booking_notes: Grilled cheese works as a late-night snack, lunch, or even canapés (cut into soldiers). Fondue station is our premium offering. All cheese sourced from British and European artisan producers.

name: Java Cart
short_description: Third-wave coffee from a hand-built oak cart. No pods, no instant, no compromise.
long_description: Our cart is built from English oak and brass, it weighs a ton (literally), and it makes the best espresso at any event in London. We use a La Marzocca GS3, beans from Workshop and Assembly on rotation, and our baristas have collectively spent more time dialling in grinders than most people spend at work. We do corporate mornings, wedding afternoon pick-me-ups, and the occasional very fancy birthday where someone just wants really good coffee. We also do pour-over for the nerds, cold brew in summer, and a chai latte that's made from real spices, not a syrup.
pricing_notes: From £350 for 2 hours. Unlimited packages from £5 per head. Pastry and cake add-ons available through partners.
setup_requirements: 1.5m x 1m space. One 13amp socket. Indoor or outdoor. We bring filtered water and all equipment.
peak_season: Year-round — coffee doesn't have an off-season
reviews_sample: Finally, proper coffee at a corporate event. Our team was very grateful. — Lisa, corporate
The oak cart is gorgeous. Looked perfect at our rustic wedding. — Emily, wedding
booking_notes: Can do espresso martini add-on for evening events. Latte art on every cup. Branded cups available for corporate.

name: Tacos el Padrino
short_description: Birria tacos, quesadillas, and horchata. Mexican comfort food from a family kitchen.
long_description: Every Saturday morning, we braise 40kg of beef shin in a chilli and spice consommé for our birria tacos. It's a recipe from Jalisco that came to London via Diego's grandmother, through his mother, and now through a truck parked wherever someone's having a party. The tacos get dipped in the fat from the consommé, griddled until crispy, stuffed with the shredded beef, and served with a cup of the broth for dipping. It's messy, it's rich, and it's the kind of food that makes you close your eyes. We also do quesadillas (proper ones, with Oaxacan string cheese), a battered fish taco that's light and perfect, and horchata made with real cinnamon and rice milk.
pricing_notes: £10-14 per head for 3 tacos and sides. Minimum spend £500. Horchata add-on £2 per head.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m for the truck. Self-contained. Outdoor or covered area.
peak_season: Year-round — birria is comfort food
signature_items: Battered fish taco with chipotle mayo
founder_story: Diego's grandmother's birria recipe survived three generations and one transatlantic move. He wasn't about to let it die in a desk job.
reviews_sample: The birria tacos are a religious experience. The dipping broth is everything. — Marcus, 30th birthday
Authentic doesn't begin to cover it. Best tacos in London. — Elena, private party
booking_notes: Birria needs to be braised overnight — confirm booking 3+ days ahead. Vegan options available on request (jackfruit birria). Late-night service available.

name: Croquette Queen
short_description: Spanish croquetas, patatas bravas, and pintxos. Canapés with actual personality.
long_description: We make croquetas. That's the headline. Our jamón croquetas are made with a béchamel so thick you could stand a spoon in it, rolled, crumbed, and fried to a golden, molten-centred perfection that makes people swear out loud. We also do salt cod, mushroom & truffle, and a blue cheese & walnut number that divides rooms. Beyond croquetas, we do a full pintxos spread: patatas bravas with proper brava sauce (not ketchup with paprika), gambas al ajillo, and tortilla española cut into perfect triangles. We deliver as drop-off platters or we set up a live frying station at your event.
pricing_notes: Canapé platters from £12 per head (6 pieces). Live frying station from £400 flat fee + per head. Minimum spend £300.
setup_requirements: For drop-off: just a table. For live station: 2m x 2m, one 13amp socket for fryer. Indoor or outdoor.
peak_season: Year-round — croquetas know no season
founder_story: Ana grew up eating croquetas in her abuela's kitchen in Seville and spent 10 years perfecting the béchamel ratio.
reviews_sample: The jamón croquetas made grown adults make sounds I've never heard before. — Kate, baby shower
Best canapés we've ever had at a work event. The croquetas ran out first. — Rav, corporate
booking_notes: Live frying station is the premium option — guests love watching. Drop-off platters come with reheating instructions. All croquetas are made fresh, never frozen.

name: Gelato Village
primary_category: ice cream vans and gelato carts
short_description: Italian gelato made daily. No van — just a beautiful cart, a freezer, and obsessive quality.
long_description: We don't have a van, and that's deliberate. Our gelato cart is hand-built, fits through any door, and goes places vans can't: rooftop terraces, restaurant courtyards, marquees, living rooms. The gelato is made fresh every morning in our kitchen in Stoke Newington using a Carpigiani batch freezer, and we never carry more than six flavours because we'd rather do six perfectly than twelve adequately. Our pistachio uses Bronte pistachios from Sicily (yes, the expensive ones), the dark chocolate is 70% Valrhona, and the seasonal specials are where we show off: fig leaf in late summer, panettone at Christmas, and a burnt honey that people dream about.
pricing_notes: From £350 for 2 hours (up to 60 scoops). Premium flavours priced at £4.50 per scoop. Wedding packages from £8 per head.
setup_requirements: Cart fits through standard doorway. Need flat surface and shade if outdoor. Power not needed — cart is insulated.
peak_season: June to September
founder_story: Marco trained at a gelateria in Bologna and moved to London with a Carpigiani and a dream.
reviews_sample: The Bronte pistachio is the best gelato I've had outside Italy. And I go to Italy a lot. — Phoebe, wedding
The cart is so elegant — it fitted perfectly into our intimate garden party. — Luca, anniversary
booking_notes: Best for intimate events — we max at 100 guests. Custom flavours for weddings with 3 weeks notice. All sorbets are vegan and dairy-free.

name: Wing Man
short_description: Chicken wings in 12 flavours. Messy, loud, and absolutely brilliant.
long_description: We do chicken wings. Just wings. Twelve flavours ranging from mild (lemon & herb, honey mustard) to certifiably insane (Carolina reaper, our 'Sign a Waiver' sauce). Wings are fried twice for maximum crunch, then tossed in your chosen glaze. We serve them in baskets with blue cheese dip, celery sticks, and a stack of wet wipes because you will need them. The truck has a leaderboard for anyone brave enough to try the reaper wings, and we play hip-hop loud enough that nobody can hear you crying. We're perfect for festivals, stag dos, and anyone who thinks a party isn't a party without sticky fingers.
pricing_notes: £8-12 per head for wings and sides. Minimum spend £400. Challenge menu (reaper wings) at your own risk.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m for the truck. Need 13amp socket for fryer. Outdoor or well-ventilated.
peak_season: Year-round — wings are forever
reviews_sample: Twelve flavours and we tried them all. The sriracha honey is my favourite thing in the world. — Dave, festival
Best late-night food at a party ever. The reaper wings nearly killed my brother. — Ash, stag do
booking_notes: Halal chicken. Reaper wing challenge available for brave events. We bring wet wipes, paper towels, and no judgement. Late-night service until 1am.

name: Press & Bloom
short_description: Botanical cocktails and cold-pressed juice bar. Grown-up drinks for grown-up events.
long_description: We're a cocktail bar with a conscience. Every cocktail on our menu uses cold-pressed juices, house-made syrups, and botanicals we grow on an allotment in Tottenham (yes, really). The Lavender Collins uses lavender we dried ourselves, the Beetroot Negroni gets its colour from actual beetroot, and the non-alcoholic menu is just as considered — no one gets a sad lime and soda. The bar is a brass-and-marble setup that looks like it belongs in a boutique hotel, staffed by bartenders who can hold a conversation and pour a drink at the same time. We're popular with weddings that want something more interesting than prosecco.
pricing_notes: From £700 for 3 hours with 2 bartenders. £14-18 per head for unlimited cocktails. Non-alcoholic packages from £8 per head.
