setup_requirements: 2m x 1.5m for the bar. One 13amp socket for fridge. Indoor or outdoor. We bring all glassware and garnishes.
peak_season: Wedding season and Christmas
founder_story: Former bartender turned urban farmer. She grows half the ingredients on her allotment and forages the rest.
reviews_sample: The most beautiful cocktails I've ever seen. And they taste even better. The lavender one is divine. — Meg, wedding
The non-alcoholic menu was so good that several drinkers switched. That never happens. — Jo, corporate event
booking_notes: Bespoke menu consultation for all events. Non-alcoholic menu always available and always excellent. All syrups and juices made in-house.

name: Slice Girls
short_description: New York-style pizza by the slice from a graffiti-covered truck. Big, foldable, and unapologetic.
long_description: We don't do Neapolitan. We do New York. Our pizzas are 20-inch, baked in a deck oven (not wood-fired — heresy, we know), with a thin, crispy, foldable crust that lets the toppings do the talking. A slice of our pepperoni — with pools of orange grease sitting in the curl of each cup — is the most satisfying single bite of food in London. We top it with full-fat mozzarella (not fior di latte, not burrata, MOZZARELLA), and we don't apologise for it. The truck is covered in street art by a local artist in Hackney, and we blast 90s hip-hop because that's the vibe. We serve fast, we serve late, and we never run out.
pricing_notes: £10-13 per head for unlimited slices. Minimum spend £500. By-the-slice pricing for festivals (£3-4 per slice).
setup_requirements: 5m x 3m for the truck. Self-contained with generator. Outdoor only.
peak_season: Summer festivals, but we do year-round
founder_story: Two sisters who spent a summer eating their way through Brooklyn and came back determined to bring proper NY-style pizza to London.
reviews_sample: Finally, proper New York pizza in London. The pepperoni with the curly cups is perfect. — Matt, festival
Fed 200 people in 90 minutes. Fast, delicious, zero waste. — Kim, corporate event
booking_notes: We serve FAST — perfect for festivals and late-night. Slices not whole pies. Vegan cheese available. The truck is very Instagrammable with the graffiti art.

name: The Brownie Post
short_description: Absurdly good brownies delivered in boxes or served from a cart. Warning: addictive.
long_description: We make one thing — brownies — and we make them devastatingly well. Our classic is a dark chocolate brownie with a crackly top and a fudgy centre that's set so precisely it wobbles when you cut it. Then we got creative: salted caramel with a caramel ripple, peanut butter with a Reese's-style layer, Biscoff with actual crushed biscuits, and a monthly special that keeps our regulars refreshing Instagram. For events, we do brownie towers (instead of cakes), brownie boxes (instead of favours), and a live brownie bar where guests choose their toppings (ice cream, sauce, cream, sprinkles). We deliver across London or set up at your event.
pricing_notes: Brownie boxes from £150 (24 brownies). Live brownie bar from £6 per head. Brownie tower (wedding cake alternative) from £200.
setup_requirements: For delivery: nothing. For live bar: 2m x 1m table space, no power needed.
peak_season: Year-round, busiest at Christmas and Valentine's
founder_story: Started baking brownies in lockdown, posted on Instagram, got 50 orders in a week, quit her marketing job, and hasn't looked back.
reviews_sample: The brownie tower replaced our wedding cake and it was the best decision we made. — Emma, wedding
Ordered brownie boxes as corporate gifts. 47 thank-you emails. — Alex, corporate
The Biscoff brownie is dangerous. I've ordered four boxes this month. — Jess, personal order
booking_notes: Brownie towers are a brilliant wedding cake alternative — much cheaper, everyone gets a slice, and they look gorgeous stacked. Free tasting for wedding orders. Next-day delivery available.

name: Frying Squad
short_description: Fish and chips from a proper chippy on wheels. Cod, haddock, and mushy peas, done properly.
long_description: We're a mobile fish and chip shop. That sentence doesn't sound exciting until you've had our twice-fried chips (blanched, rested, fried again — crispy outside, fluffy inside) with a piece of sustainably sourced cod in a beer batter that shatters when you bite it. We serve on proper paper, with curry sauce, mushy peas, tartare sauce, and pickled onions. It's traditional, it's comforting, and it makes people irrationally happy. We've done everything from black-tie corporate events (fish and chips in evening wear is surprisingly classy) to school fêtes where we served 300 portions and ran out of nothing.
pricing_notes: £10-13 per head for fish, chips, and sides. Minimum spend £500. Mini portions for children £5.
setup_requirements: 5m x 3m for the van. Need 2x 13amp sockets for fryers. Outdoor or very well-ventilated.
peak_season: Year-round — fish and chips is a national constant
founder_story: Third-generation chippy family from Essex who decided to take the fryer on the road.
reviews_sample: Fish and chips at our evening wedding reception. Everyone was SO happy. — Rachel, wedding
Best chips I've ever had. The double-fry thing works. — Ian, corporate summer party
Fed 250 at a school fête without breaking a sweat. Proper operation. — Kim, school fête
booking_notes: Sustainable MSC-certified fish. Gluten-free batter available on request. Kids' portions available. We leave the site spotless — no oil smells.

name: Little Dumpling
primary_category: bao, dumplings, and Asian street food
short_description: Hand-folded dumplings with Sichuan chilli oil. Warning: extremely moreish.
long_description: We make dumplings by hand every morning — pork & ginger jiaozi, prawn har gow, and a mushroom & truffle number for vegetarians that's as good as anything with meat. The wrappers are thin enough to see through, each one folded with 18 pleats (we're not as obsessive as the momo place, but we're close). They're steamed in bamboo baskets or pan-fried until the bottoms are golden and crunchy. But the real star is our Sichuan chilli oil — we make it weekly with dried chillies, Sichuan peppercorns, star anise, and sesame, and people literally bring containers to take it home. We also do a dan dan noodle bowl that's become a corporate lunch staple.
pricing_notes: £10-14 per head for 8-10 dumplings and sides. Minimum spend £400. Dan dan noodle add-on £5 per head.
setup_requirements: 3m x 2m space. One 13amp socket for steamer. Indoor or outdoor.
peak_season: Year-round
founder_story: Dim sum chef from a restaurant in Chinatown who wanted to bring the craft of dumpling-making to events where people could actually watch.
reviews_sample: The chilli oil. THE CHILLI OIL. I bought three jars. — Lex, birthday party
Best corporate lunch we've had. Simple, elegant, delicious. — Sarah, corporate
booking_notes: Chilli oil available to purchase separately (popular as event favours). Dumpling-making workshops available for team-building events (£25 per person).

name: Naan Stop
short_description: Naan wraps, tandoori chicken, and mango lassi. Indian street food that never stops moving.
long_description: We take everything great about an Indian takeaway and serve it from a truck, faster and fresher. Our naan wraps are the core — warm, soft naan filled with tandoori chicken (marinated overnight in yoghurt and spices), pickled onion, raita, and our green chutney. We also do a lamb seekh kebab wrap, a paneer tikka version, and a chana masala wrap for vegans. The tandoor is front and centre in the truck — guests can see the chicken sizzling and the naans puffing up, and the smell alone draws a queue. We're built for volume: we've done 500-person festivals and still had food left.
pricing_notes: £8-12 per head for wrap and drink. Minimum spend £500. Mango lassi add-on £3.
setup_requirements: 5m x 3m for the truck. Self-contained with gas. Outdoor only.
peak_season: Festival season (May-Sep) but year-round
founder_story: Former restaurant manager who noticed that the best Indian food was locked inside restaurants and wanted to take it to where people actually are.
reviews_sample: Fed 300 people at our Eid celebration. Fast, delicious, halal. Perfect. — Ayesha, Eid party
The tandoori chicken wrap is insanely good for the price. Best festival food ever. — Mike, festival
booking_notes: Halal certified. Built for high-volume — can serve 300+ in 2 hours. Mango lassi is our upsell and it works every time.

name: Milk Bar
primary_category: ice cream vans and gelato carts
short_description: Soft serve, milkshakes, and cereal milk ice cream. Nostalgic, fun, and slightly unhinged.
long_description: We do soft serve the way it should be — insanely creamy, swirled high, and covered in toppings that have no business being on ice cream (but absolutely should be). Our base flavours are vanilla, chocolate, and a rotating special, but the magic is in the toppings bar: crushed Oreos, honeycomb, brownie bits, mochi pieces, matcha powder, salted caramel sauce, and a cereal milk drizzle inspired by a certain New York bakery. Milkshakes are thick enough to stand a straw in, and we do a 'freakshake' for events that's essentially a sundae, a milkshake, and a brownie combined in a jar. The van is mint green with neon signage and a toppings bar that looks like a pick 'n' mix.
pricing_notes: From £350 for 2 hours. Soft serve from £4 per head. Milkshakes £5 each. Freakshakes £8 each.
setup_requirements: Vehicle access. Flat ground. Self-contained. Outdoor or large indoor space.
peak_season: Summer, but we do indoor winter events too
signature_items: Vanilla soft serve with toppings bar
Freakshake (soft serve + brownie + shake in a jar)
reviews_sample: The toppings bar! Kids (and adults) went absolutely mad. Best thing at the party. — Cath, birthday party
The freakshake is completely over the top and I love it. — Leo, festival
booking_notes: Toppings bar is self-service — guests love it. Vegan soft serve available. Neon signs included for photo opportunities.

name: Coal Yard Kitchen
short_description: Argentine-style open fire cooking. Whole lamb, grilled vegetables, and chimichurri on everything.
long_description: We cook over fire. Not in a smoker, not on a gas BBQ — over actual burning logs on an adjustable iron grill (parrilla) that we built ourselves. Our thing is the whole lamb: butterflied, salt-crusted, cooked slowly over embers for 6 hours until it's pink inside with a charred, salty crust. We carve it in front of your guests, which is the kind of spectacle that makes people forget about their phones for five minutes. We also do whole chickens, beef ribs, and a grilled vegetable spread that includes coal-roasted aubergines, peppers, and courgettes with chimichurri. Everything tastes of smoke and fire and outdoors.
pricing_notes: Whole lamb from £1,200 (feeds 60-80). Full menu from £25 per head. Minimum spend £1,200.
setup_requirements: Large outdoor space — 8m x 4m minimum. Fire pit/parrilla setup. We need early access (6am for evening service). Outdoor only.
peak_season: Summer, but we love a winter fire feast
founder_story: Spent two years working on estancias in Patagonia, came back with a parrilla and a deep love for fire-cooked meat.
reviews_sample: The whole lamb being carved was the highlight of our wedding. Gasps from the crowd. — Jo, wedding
Fire cooking outside in January. Mad, cold, and completely brilliant. — Steve, birthday party
booking_notes: We need early access for fire setup. Whole lamb feeds 60-80 — order based on guest count. Vegetable-only parrilla available for mixed dietary events. The fire itself is a feature — position it where guests can watch.

name: Mother Clucker
short_description: Fried chicken sandwiches with attitude. Brined, buttermilked, double-dredged, and dangerously good.
long_description: Our chicken goes through a three-day process before it hits the fryer. Day one: brined in salt and spice water. Day two: buttermilked overnight. Day three: double-dredged in seasoned flour and fried at exactly 170°C until the coating is shattering-crispy and the inside is juicy enough to run down your arm. It goes in a brioche bun with pickled cabbage, ranch, and hot sauce. That's the classic. The Nashville Hot version adds cayenne oil and pickles. The Korean version gets gochujang mayo and pickled daikon. We're not subtle, we're not healthy, and we're not sorry.
pricing_notes: £10-14 per head for sandwich, fries, and slaw. Minimum spend £500.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m for the truck. Two 13amp sockets. Outdoor or well-ventilated indoor.
peak_season: Year-round
signature_items: The Classic (buttermilk fried chicken, pickled slaw, ranch)
reviews_sample: Three-day brine process and you can TASTE it. Best fried chicken in London. — Joe, festival
Late-night fried chicken at our wedding was the smartest thing we did. — Tash, wedding
booking_notes: Halal chicken available. Nashville Hot is genuinely very hot — we warn people. Late-night service until midnight. We fry fast — 200+ sandwiches per hour.

name: Baba Ganoush
short_description: Charcoal-grilled mezze, loaded falafel, and the most moreish baba ganoush in London.
long_description: Everything we serve has been near a flame. Our aubergines are charred whole over charcoal until the skin is black and the inside is molten — that's where the baba ganoush starts, and it's smoky, silky, and obsessively good. Our falafel is herb-heavy (more coriander and parsley than chickpea, almost), fried to order, and served in warm pita with everything: tahini, amba, pickled chilli, tomato, and a fistful of fresh herbs. We also do lamb kofta on the charcoal grill, chicken shawarma, and a mezze spread that covers an entire table. We're the Middle Eastern food that makes people rethink what they thought they knew about hummus.
pricing_notes: £9-13 per head. Minimum spend £400. Full mezze spread from £16 per head.
setup_requirements: 3m x 3m space. Charcoal grill (we bring our own). Outdoor only for grilling, indoor for mezze-only events.
peak_season: Summer for grilling, year-round for mezze
signature_items: Lamb kofta from the charcoal grill
founder_story: Karim's family runs a restaurant in Beirut. He brought the charcoal grill to London because no one here was doing baba ganoush properly.
reviews_sample: The baba ganoush is worth the booking alone. So smoky and perfect. — Tess, private party
Fed 80 guests at our garden wedding. Everything was incredible, especially the kofta. — Hassan, wedding
booking_notes: Halal certified. Charcoal grilling means outdoor only for the grill, but mezze platters can be served indoors. Can pair as a starter alongside a main caterer.

name: The Crêpe Escape
short_description: Sweet and savoury crêpes from a Parisian-style cart. Galettes for lunch, Nutella for pudding.
long_description: We do crêpes properly — two batters, two menus. The sweet crêpes are classic French: thin, lacy, served with Nutella, lemon & sugar, berries & cream, or our signature salted caramel & banana. The savoury galettes use buckwheat flour (naturally gluten-free) and come filled with things like ham, Gruyère & egg, or mushroom, spinach & goat's cheese. The cart is painted in French blue with a zinc counter, and we play Serge Gainsbourg because we're committed to the bit. We're perfect as a lunch option, a dessert add-on, or a standalone for smaller events where you want something a bit different.
pricing_notes: £5-8 per head for crêpes. Savoury galettes £7-10 per head. Minimum spend £300.
setup_requirements: 2m x 2m space for the cart. One 13amp socket for billig. Indoor or outdoor.
peak_season: Year-round
founder_story: Lived in Paris for three years, missed the crêpe stands when she came home, built her own.
reviews_sample: The galettes are restaurant quality. Buckwheat batter is the real deal. — Claire, private party
Kids loved watching the crêpes being made. Simple, fun, delicious. — Hannah, school fête
booking_notes: Savoury galettes work as a lunch main. Sweet crêpes are a perfect dessert add-on. Buckwheat galettes are naturally gluten-free. Cart fits through standard doorways.

name: Pitta Perfect
short_description: Lebanese street food from a turquoise truck. Shawarma, manoushe, and the crunchiest falafel.
long_description: Our shawarma is marinated for 72 hours and stacked on a vertical spit that rotates in the truck window — it's basically a neon sign that says 'come eat'. We carve it thin, stuff it in warm pitta with toum (garlic sauce that's basically garlic mayonnaise on steroids), pickled turnip, and a drizzle of tahini. But the thing that surprises people is our manoushe — a Lebanese flatbread topped with za'atar and olive oil, baked in our deck oven in 2 minutes, and served hot and fragrant. It's like pizza's cooler, simpler cousin. We also do a fattoush that uses our day-old pitta fried into croutons, because wasting bread is a sin we take seriously.
pricing_notes: £8-12 per head. Minimum spend £450. Manoushe station add-on from £5 per head. Mezze platters £6 per head.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m for the truck. Self-contained. Outdoor or covered area.
peak_season: Year-round
reviews_sample: The manoushe is so simple and so perfect. Za'atar and olive oil — that's it. Genius. — Sami, private party
Fast, tasty, affordable. Fed 100 people at our company BBQ and everyone was impressed. — Laura, corporate
booking_notes: Halal certified. Manoushe station is our secret weapon — highly recommend adding it. Can serve 200+ in under 2 hours.

name: Proper Pies
short_description: Handmade pies with buttery shortcrust and fillings that take all day. Proper comfort.
long_description: Every pie we make starts at 5am with butter, flour, and cold hands. Our pastry is short, flaky, and golden — none of that pale, soggy-bottomed nonsense. The fillings are slow-cooked: our steak & kidney uses shin braised in stout for four hours, the chicken & mushroom has a tarragon cream sauce that smells like Sunday, and our vegan jackfruit & peppercorn pie has convinced several hardcore carnivores to reconsider their position. We serve with creamy mash, liquor (the proper parsley sauce, not the drink), and mushy peas. For events we do a pie bar where guests choose their filling — it's simple, it's British, and it works every single time.
pricing_notes: £9-13 per head for pie, mash, and sides. Minimum spend £350. Mini pies as canapés £3 each.
setup_requirements: Kitchen access or 2x 13amp sockets for warming. Table for pie bar setup. Indoor or covered outdoor.
peak_season: October to March, but pies work year-round
founder_story: Former City trader who quit finance to make pies full-time. Says he's never been happier or less wealthy.
reviews_sample: Pie and mash at a funeral wake — it's what he would have wanted, and it was perfect. — Jane, wake
The pie bar was genius. Everyone arguing about which filling is best. Steak & kidney won. — Tom, wedding
booking_notes: Mini pies work brilliantly as canapés. Pie bar is our most popular setup. Can do bespoke fillings for larger events.

name: Bangers & Bash
short_description: Gourmet sausages, creamy mash, and onion gravy. British comfort food, done loud.
long_description: We do sausages. Exceptional sausages. Our butcher in Bermondsey makes them to our spec: coarse-ground, natural casing, no rusk. The classic pork & fennel is our bestseller, but the wild boar & apple is the dark horse, and the vegan beetroot & black bean has won over people who swore they'd never eat a non-meat sausage. Every sausage is char-grilled on our plancha and served with silky mash (Maris Pipers, real butter, don't ask about the calories), proper onion gravy, and a choice of mustards. We set up a serving station that looks like a posh British pub, complete with wooden boards and metal camping cups for the gravy.
pricing_notes: £9-12 per head for 2 sausages, mash, and gravy. Minimum spend £400. Hot dog service available for faster turnaround.
setup_requirements: 3m x 2m for serving station. One 13amp socket. Indoor or outdoor with plancha.
peak_season: Bonfire Night, winter months, but honestly any time
reviews_sample: Sausage and mash at our Bonfire Night party. Everyone was happy, nobody was cold. — Steve, private party
The wild boar sausage is incredible. We've rebooked for our Christmas party. — Abby, corporate
booking_notes: Hot dog service is faster for large numbers. Vegetarian and vegan sausages always available. Can do a 'build your own' station with toppings.

name: Verde
short_description: High-end plant-based catering that makes veganism look effortless. Because it should be.
long_description: We're a plant-based catering company that doesn't lead with the word 'vegan'. We lead with 'delicious' and let people figure out the rest. Our food is built on technique, not substitution — we're not replacing meat, we're cooking vegetables like they deserve to be cooked. Whole roasted celeriac with miso butter, beetroot tartare with capers and shallot, a cashew cream tiramisu that's been described as 'unfair to regular tiramisu'. For events, we do plated dinners, sharing feasts, and grazing tables that prove you don't need prosciutto to make a table look stunning. Our chef trained at The Ledbury before going plant-based.
pricing_notes: £25-40 per head for plated dinner. Sharing feast from £20 per head. Minimum spend £600. Service staff included.
setup_requirements: Kitchen access for plated service. Table space for sharing. Indoor preferred. We bring all serving ware and staff.
peak_season: Year-round — Veganuary is our busiest month
signature_items: Whole roasted celeriac with miso butter
founder_story: Former Ledbury sous chef who went vegan and realised London's event scene had nothing that matched restaurant-quality plant-based food.
reviews_sample: Nobody knew it was vegan until the speeches. THAT'S how you do it. — Nell, wedding
The celeriac was a revelation. I've never said that about a vegetable before. — James, private dinner
booking_notes: Tasting dinner for wedding clients (£85 for two, redeemable). All allergens catered for without compromising flavour. Service staff included in all packages.

name: Espresso Yourself
short_description: Mobile espresso bar with pastries from a Hackney bakery. Coffee that actually tastes like coffee.
long_description: We're a no-nonsense coffee cart. Good beans (currently on a Kenyan single origin from Origin), good milk (Brades Farm — it steams like a dream), good equipment (Linea Mini), and baristas who've worked in shops you've actually heard of. We don't do flavoured syrups or complicated menus — we do espresso, flat whites, filter, and a very good hot chocolate for the kids and the cold-handed. The pastry situation is a collaboration with a bakery in Clapton: almond croissants, pain au chocolat, and a cardamom bun that sells out first. We show up, we make coffee, and we leave. Simple.
pricing_notes: From £300 for 2 hours (up to 50 coffees). Then £4 per coffee. Pastry add-on £3 per head.
setup_requirements: 1m x 1m space. One 13amp socket. Indoor or outdoor. We bring everything.
peak_season: Year-round
reviews_sample: Simple, great coffee, no faff. Exactly what we needed for our morning-after brunch. — Dave, wedding
The cardamom buns sold out in 20 minutes. Need to order more next time. — Amy, corporate
booking_notes: Quick turnaround on bookings — can often do 48 hours notice. We keep it simple and do it well.

name: Platter Up
short_description: Drop-off platters and canapé boxes for offices, parties, and people who hate cooking.
long_description: We make beautiful food and bring it to your door. That's it. No setup, no staff, no van in your garden — just restaurant-quality platters delivered in time for your event. Our range covers everything from sushi platters and Vietnamese summer rolls to classic smoked salmon blinis and mini Yorkshire puddings with roast beef. Everything arrives on compostable trays, ready to unwrap and serve. We started because someone asked us to cater a 15-person dinner party and we realised most caterers have £1,000+ minimums. Our minimum is £100. We're the caterer for normal people having normal parties.
pricing_notes: Platters from £100 (feeds 8-10). Per head canapé boxes from £10 (6 pieces). Free delivery within 5 miles.
setup_requirements: Nothing — delivered to your door. Just need a table and a fridge.
peak_season: Christmas party season and summer
signature_items: Vietnamese summer rolls with peanut dip
Mini Yorkshire puddings with rare beef
founder_story: Started delivering platters to friends during lockdown. Turns out everyone wants nice food without the stress of cooking.
reviews_sample: Ordered for a work lunch — beautiful presentation, great variety, half the price of other caterers. — Mel, corporate
Perfect for a small christening. No fuss, everything looked gorgeous. — Katie, christening
booking_notes: Minimum order £100. Same-day delivery sometimes possible. Custom menus for events over £300. Everything arrives ready to serve — just unwrap.

name: Gin & Bear It
short_description: G&T bar with 40+ gins and a bartender who knows them all. Plus cocktails on tap.
long_description: We built a bar inside an Airstream trailer and filled it with 40 gins from British distilleries you've never heard of. Our bartenders don't just pour — they ask what you like, recommend a gin, choose the tonic, and garnish it properly (not just a sad slice of lemon). We also do cocktails on tap: pre-batched Aperol spritzes, espresso martinis, and a passion fruit margarita that sells out at every wedding we do. The Airstream is polished aluminium with Edison bulbs inside, and it looks stunning in a field, a garden, or a car park. We handle all the licensing paperwork, and our bartenders know when to pour strong and when to pour subtle.
pricing_notes: From £750 for 3 hours with 2 bartenders. Unlimited G&T packages from £15 per head. Cash bar option available.
setup_requirements: Vehicle access for Airstream. Flat ground. Self-contained with generator. Outdoor or very large indoor.
peak_season: Summer weddings and Christmas parties
founder_story: Bought a rusting Airstream on eBay, spent a year restoring it, and now it's the most popular mobile bar in south London.
reviews_sample: The Airstream was STUNNING at our wedding. Bartenders were brilliant — they remembered everyone's drink. — Fran, wedding
Gin tasting at our hen do. So much better than a cocktail-making class. — Bex, hen party
booking_notes: Licensed — we handle all TEN paperwork. Airstream is very popular for weddings — book 3+ months ahead. Non-alcoholic menu always available. Can provide branded gin bottles as favours.

name: The Samosa Company
short_description: Hand-folded samosas in 15 flavours. From lamb keema to chocolate & hazelnut. Seriously.
long_description: We make samosas. A lot of samosas. Our kitchen in Leyton folds 3,000+ a week, each one by hand, each one crimped shut with a technique that's been in Meera's family for four generations. The classics are perfect: lamb keema with peas, aloo gobi, and paneer & spinach. But we also do unexpected flavours that shouldn't work but absolutely do: mushroom & truffle, pulled pork with BBQ sauce, and a chocolate & hazelnut dessert samosa that has caused actual arguments at events. For events we do a samosa bar (choose your filling, we fry it fresh) or drop-off platters with chutney selection. We're the ultimate canapé.
pricing_notes: Platters from £200 (48 samosas). Live frying station from £400. Per head from £6 (4 samosas with chutneys).
setup_requirements: For drop-off: nothing. For live station: 2m x 2m, one 13amp socket for fryer. Indoor or outdoor.
peak_season: Diwali season and Christmas party season
founder_story: Meera's grandmother taught her to fold samosas at age 8 in Leicester. She now makes 3,000 a week in London and her grandmother approves of every single flavour (except the chocolate one).
reviews_sample: Samosa bar at our Diwali party was the best decision. 15 flavours and people tried every one. — Anish, Diwali party
Drop-off platters for our office — 200 samosas gone in 20 minutes. Ordering double next time. — Kate, corporate
The chocolate samosa is insane. My kids ask for them instead of birthday cake. — Deepa, birthday
booking_notes: Drop-off available with 48-hour notice. Live frying station is the premium experience. Halal certified. Can do mini samosas for canapé service. Corporate accounts available for regular orders.

name: Salt Beef & Sons
short_description: Salt beef bagels, latkes, and pickles from a family deli on wheels.
long_description: We've been curing beef for three generations — our brisket sits in a pink salt cure for 10 days, then gets slowly simmered until it's tender, salty, and as pink as a sunset. We slice it thick, pile it into a fresh beigel (not bagel — we're East End, it's a beigel), add English mustard and gherkins, and hand it over. That's been the recipe since 1958, when grandad had a stall on Brick Lane. We've now got a truck that does the rounds at weddings, bar mitzvahs, and late-night events where a salt beef beigel at midnight is exactly what everyone needs. We also do latkes, chopped liver, and a chicken soup that cures everything.
pricing_notes: £8-12 per head for beigel and sides. Minimum spend £400. Late-night beigel service from £6 per head.
setup_requirements: 3m x 2m for the serving setup. No power needed for cold-cut service. Indoor or outdoor.
peak_season: Year-round — salt beef doesn't have an off-season
signature_items: Salt beef beigel with mustard & gherkin
founder_story: Third-generation salt beef curers from the East End. The recipe hasn't changed since 1958 and they have no plans to fix what isn't broken.
reviews_sample: Late-night salt beef beigels at our wedding. The queue was 30 deep and nobody complained. — David, wedding
Chicken soup at a winter birthday party. Everyone felt looked after. — Ruth, 60th birthday
booking_notes: Salt beef needs 10 days lead time (curing process). Late-night service is our speciality. Can do kosher on request with advance notice.

name: Wok This Way
primary_category: bao, dumplings, and Asian street food
short_description: Wok-fried noodles, pad thai, and Asian salads tossed in front of your guests.
long_description: We bring a double wok burner to your event and cook everything live. The theatrics of a flaming wok — the toss, the sizzle, the 3-foot flame that makes people jump back — is half the point. The food is the other half: pad thai with tamarind and crushed peanuts, Singapore noodles that actually taste of something, and a chilli basil chicken stir-fry that's our most requested dish at every event. We also do a build-your-own noodle bar where guests choose their protein, veg, noodle type, and sauce, and we wok it up in 90 seconds. It's fast, it's fun, and the queue is part of the entertainment.
pricing_notes: £10-14 per head for noodle dish and side. Minimum spend £500. Build-your-own noodle bar from £12 per head.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m outdoor space for wok burners (fire risk — outdoor only). We bring our own gas, woks, and extraction.
peak_season: Year-round
signature_items: Pad thai with tamarind & crushed peanuts
reviews_sample: The flames from the wok had the kids transfixed. And the pad thai was brilliant. — Laura, birthday party
Build-your-own noodle bar at our team party. Interactive, fast, and delicious. — Rob, corporate
booking_notes: Outdoor only due to wok flames. Build-your-own noodle bar is our bestseller for corporate events. We cook fast — can serve 200+ in under 2 hours.

name: The Taco Truck
short_description: No-frills tacos from a truck that's been everywhere. Honest Mexican food, honest prices.
long_description: We've been doing tacos from this truck since 2019. It's not pretty — it's dented, the paint is peeling, and the menu is written on a chalkboard in handwriting that only we can read. But the tacos are exceptional. Our carne asada (skirt steak, chargrilled, sliced thin) is marinated in lime, chilli, and garlic overnight. The chicken tinga is slow-braised with chipotle and tomato until it shreds with a look. The bean & cheese is the vegetarian option and it outsells everything else at school fêtes. We use nixtamal corn tortillas from a masa supplier in Brixton, and we double-stack them because single tortillas are a structural liability.
pricing_notes: £9-13 per head for 3 tacos and sides. Minimum spend £450.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m for the truck. Self-contained. Outdoor or covered.
peak_season: Summer, but we work year-round
reviews_sample: Best value taco truck in London. No pretension, just really good tacos. — Mark, festival
The carne asada is perfection. Simple and brilliant. — Rosa, private party
booking_notes: Quick turnaround on bookings — can often do 5 days notice. No-frills setup but the food speaks for itself. Double tortillas always.

name: Doughnut Time
short_description: Filled doughnuts glazed to order. Brioche style, not ring. Each one is a small event.
long_description: We fry brioche doughnuts and fill them with things that have no business being in a doughnut — and it works every time. Our classic is a vanilla custard with a crème brûlée glaze (we actually blowtorch it in front of you). The salted caramel oozes. The raspberry & white chocolate is pink and ridiculous. And the monthly special keeps our regulars in a constant state of anticipation (past hits: Biscoff cheesecake, pistachio & rose, miso caramel). For events, we do a doughnut wall (they hang on pegs — very photogenic), a glazing station where guests choose their topping, or straight-up boxes delivered warm.
pricing_notes: Doughnut boxes from £250 (24 doughnuts). Doughnut wall from £350 (36 doughnuts). Live glazing station from £6 per head.
setup_requirements: For delivery/wall: nothing. For live station: 2m x 2m, one 13amp socket for fryer. Indoor or outdoor.
peak_season: Year-round
founder_story: Started in a home kitchen during lockdown. First Instagram post got 200 DMs. Bought a fryer that week.
reviews_sample: The doughnut wall at our wedding was the most photographed thing there. Including the bride. — Jo, wedding
Crème brûlée doughnut blowtorched in front of me. Life-changing. — Sam, birthday party
booking_notes: Doughnut walls are our most popular wedding item. Live glazing is the premium experience. Vegan doughnuts always available. Can do corporate branding on boxes.

name: Grazing & Grace
short_description: Curated grazing boards with a seasonal, farm-to-table philosophy. Nothing on our boards is ordinary.
long_description: We don't do 'nice cheese on a board'. We do researched, seasonal, story-driven grazing. Every board comes with tasting notes — where the cheese is from, who made the chutney, why we chose that particular honey. Our produce comes from farms we've visited: the goat's cheese is from a family in Kent, the sourdough crackers are baked by a woman in Peckham, and the fig jam is made in our own kitchen from figs that grow on our allotment. For larger events we build themed tables: the 'British Isles' board features only UK producers, the 'Mediterranean' travels from Andalusia to Lebanon, and the 'Vegan Feast' proves that a board without cheese can still make people gather round.
pricing_notes: From £18 per head for a full grazing board. Individual boards from £250. Themed tables from £25 per head.
setup_requirements: Table or surface. Indoor preferred (cheese doesn't love direct sun). Access 1.5 hours before.
peak_season: Wedding season and Christmas
founder_story: Former cheese buyer for a department store who wanted to tell the stories behind the producers she discovered.
reviews_sample: The tasting notes for each cheese were such a lovely touch. Guests were reading them like a wine menu. — Lucy, wedding
The vegan board was genuinely stunning. Nobody missed the cheese. — Kate, baby shower
booking_notes: Tasting notes included with every board. Can coordinate with florists for styled tables. All packaging is compostable. Free consultation for events over £400.

name: The Pizza Project
short_description: Community pizza nights and event catering from a trailer built by hand. Sourdough, wood-fired, and proper.
long_description: We built our pizza trailer in a workshop in Tottenham over six months — every plank, every hinge, every tile. It's our proudest possession and it makes 400+ pizzas every weekend across London. Our dough is a 48-hour sourdough (the starter is 3 years old and has a name — Margaret), topped with San Marzano, fior di latte, and seasonal ingredients from the farmers' market down the road. We do regular community pizza nights in our local park (BYOB, bring a blanket), and for private events we bring the same energy: wood smoke, good music, and unlimited pizza that keeps coming until everyone's full or asleep.
pricing_notes: £12-15 per head for unlimited pizza. Minimum spend £550. Includes salad and garlic bread.
setup_requirements: 5m x 3m outdoor space. Self-contained with wood-fired oven. Outdoor only.
peak_season: May to September, but we do winter events in covered venues
founder_story: Two friends who built a pizza trailer by hand and accidentally started a business. Margaret the sourdough starter is the silent third partner.
reviews_sample: The community pizza night energy carried over perfectly to our wedding. Relaxed, fun, and SO much pizza. — Liv, wedding
Margaret the sourdough starter is 3 years old and she's doing great work. Best pizza crust I've had. — Andy, private party
booking_notes: Margaret (the starter) needs to be happy, which means we need confirmed numbers 5 days ahead. Gluten-free bases available. We run community pizza nights in Tottenham — come try before you book.

name: Brew & Chew
short_description: Coffee in the morning, smash burgers at night. One truck, two lives.
long_description: By day we're a speciality coffee cart — Assembly beans, oat milk, proper latte art. By night we flip burgers on a flat-top that gets so hot the cheese melts on contact. The concept sounds mad but it works: we do wedding mornings (brunch coffee and pastries), then switch to evening burgers (smash patties, secret sauce, American cheese). It means you can book one vendor for two services and save the hassle of coordinating multiples. Our setup converts in about 30 minutes — espresso machine goes down, plancha comes up, and the menu switches from cortados to double cheeseburgers.
pricing_notes: Coffee service from £300 for 2 hours. Burger service from £500 for 2 hours. Combined day-night package from £700.
setup_requirements: 3m x 2m space. Two 13amp sockets. Indoor or outdoor.
peak_season: Wedding season
signature_items: Double smash burger with secret sauce
founder_story: Barista by trade, burger obsessive by nature. Couldn't choose between the two passions, so didn't.
reviews_sample: Coffee for our morning-after brunch, burgers for the evening do. One booking, two services. Genius. — Tom, wedding
The day-night concept is brilliant. Coffee was excellent, burgers were even better. — Jess, corporate
booking_notes: The combined package is our bestseller for weddings. We need 30 min between services to switch setup. Can do late-night burger service until midnight.

name: The Gravy Boat
short_description: Sunday roast dinners served from a canal boat. No, really. A canal boat.
long_description: We cook Sunday roasts on a narrowboat called The Gravy Boat and serve them dockside. The boat has a full kitchen — we roast whole chickens, shoulders of lamb, and our famous beef sirloin on board, carve them at a serving station on the towpath, and plate up with Yorkshire puddings (risen high, crunchy edges), roast potatoes (goose fat, obviously), seasonal veg, and proper gravy made from the roasting tray. It's surreal and charming and smells incredible from 50 metres away. We moor up wherever you need us — canal-side venues, pub gardens near the water, even private moorings. If you've got a canal, we've got Sunday lunch.
pricing_notes: £16-22 per head for full roast. Minimum spend £500. Maximum 80 guests (boat kitchen capacity).
setup_requirements: Canal mooring. We need to moor 3 hours before service. Serving happens on towpath — need table space. Weather dependent for outdoor dining.
peak_season: Spring and summer (al fresco canal dining)
signature_items: Whole roasted chicken with lemon & thyme
founder_story: Bought a narrowboat to live on, accidentally started cooking Sunday roasts for the neighbours on the towpath, and it grew from there.
reviews_sample: A canal boat roast dinner for our anniversary. Most unique dining experience we've ever had. — Richard, anniversary
The Yorkshire puddings made on a BOAT. I can't explain how charming this is. — Sophie, birthday
booking_notes: Canal access required — check mooring availability with us before booking. Maximum 80 guests due to boat kitchen size. Weather backup plan recommended for outdoor towpath dining.

name: Vegan Feast
short_description: Plant-based comfort food from a truck. Burgers, loaded fries, and fried 'chicken' that fools everyone.
long_description: We make junk food that happens to be vegan. Our seitan fried 'chicken' burger has fooled actual chicken farmers (we have witnesses), the smash burger uses a pea protein patty that sizzles and chars like beef, and our loaded fries come with a cashew cheese sauce that's better than most dairy versions. We're not trying to be healthy — we're trying to be delicious, and the fact that it's all plants is a bonus. The truck is graffitied with vegetables wearing sunglasses (don't ask) and we play the kind of music that makes vegetable-based dining feel less like a compromise and more like a party.
pricing_notes: £10-14 per head. Minimum spend £450. Late-night menu from £8 per head.
setup_requirements: 4m x 3m for the truck. One 13amp socket for fryers. Outdoor or well-ventilated indoor.
peak_season: Veganuary and summer festivals
founder_story: Chef who went vegan and got annoyed that 'vegan street food' meant a sad falafel wrap. Built a truck to prove junk food doesn't need animals.
reviews_sample: My meat-eating husband couldn't tell the 'chicken' burger wasn't chicken. Result. — Amy, private party
Best vegan junk food I've ever had. The loaded fries are criminal. — Leo, festival
booking_notes: 100% plant-based kitchen — zero cross-contamination. Can pair alongside a non-vegan vendor. Late-night service available. The truck looks amazing — great for photos.
